articles.title_orig: EXPLAINER - How China is reshaping its export map beyond the US
articles.title_zh: EXPLAINER - How China is reshaping its export map beyond the US
articles.content_orig:
China sold more goods to the world despite a sharp drop in exports to the US last year, as stronger demand from Southeast Asia and Europe more than made up for lost American sales.
The growth came against the backdrop of a trade conflict that escalated in 2018, when President Donald Trump's first administration imposed additional tariffs on Chinese goods, citing concerns over intellectual property and pressure on American companies to transfer technology.
The dispute intensified in April 2025 as both countries announced successive tariff increases.
Talks in Geneva the following month brought a temporary easing, with both sides agreeing to remove some additional duties and suspend others for an initial 90 days. The agreement did not eliminate all tariffs between them.
Tariffs are taxes paid by businesses importing goods. They can make Chinese products more expensive for American buyers, putting pressure on exporters to cut prices or find customers elsewhere.
China's exports to the US fell 19.5% in 2025, reaching approximately 3.01 trillion yuan ($420 billion). Yet its total exports rose 6.1% to around $3.77 trillion, according to customs figures.
The contrast shows how stronger sales elsewhere helped China absorb the decline in one of its biggest markets.
Southeast Asia and Europe fill the gap
Two markets provided a particularly important cushion: the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and the European Union.
Chinese exports to ASEAN rose 14% to approximately $665 billion in 2025, while shipments to the EU increased 9% to about $560 billion.
Calculations using rounded customs figures show that China gained about $128 billion in additional sales to those two markets, compared with roughly $102 billion in lost sales to the US.
In other words, the gains in Southeast Asia and Europe were about a quarter larger than the American shortfall.
ASEAN accounted for approximately $82 billion of the additional sales, while the EU contributed about $46 billion.
The figures do not mean the same goods once intended for American buyers were shipped elsewhere. They show that, across China's export sector, stronger sales in other markets outweighed the US decline.
Together, ASEAN and the EU bought around $1.23 trillion in Chinese goods last year, nearly three times the amount purchased by the US.
The two markets accounted for roughly one-third of China's exports, compared with about one-ninth for the American market.
China's trading relationships also extend well beyond those destinations.
Total trade with Africa rose 18.4% in 2025, while trade with Latin America increased 6.5%. These figures include both exports and imports.
China recorded growth in trade with more than 190 countries and regions during the year, according to the General Administration of Customs.
Trade with Belt and Road partner countries increased 6.3% to approximately $3.3 trillion, accounting for just over half of China's total goods trade.
These groups overlap, so their contributions cannot simply be added together. But the figures show the breadth of China's trading network and why falling sales in one market do not necessarily lead to lower exports overall.
Chips and electric vehicles drive further growth
China's export growth continued in 2026, supported by machinery, electronics and products such as electric vehicles and batteries.
Exports rose 16.4% in the first nine months, reaching approximately $3.45 trillion when converted using the government's published trade totals.
Mechanical and electrical products accounted for almost two-thirds of exports. Sales of those products grew 23.7%, faster than exports overall, according to the National Bureau of Statistics.
Chip exports nearly doubled, rising 99.1%. Electric vehicle exports increased 72.3%, while lithium battery exports grew 36.4%.
Equipment manufacturing accounted for nearly 90% of the increase in exports, customs figures showed.
More than half of exports were parts, materials and other goods used to make products abroad, highlighting China's role as a supplier to overseas factories as well as consumers.
The increases measure sales value, so they can reflect changes in prices as well as the number of products shipped. Strong national figures also do not mean every exporter benefited equally.
The latest data show that overall trade with the US has begun growing again alongside continued expansion elsewhere.
China's trade with ASEAN rose 22.7% to approximately $1.02 trillion in the first nine months of 2026. Trade with the EU increased 8.4% to around $711 billion, while trade with the US rose 4.1% to approximately $473 billion.
Those totals include imports and exports, so they do not show how exports alone changed.
The American market remains important, and finding more customers elsewhere does not mean Chinese businesses have stopped relying on US buyers.
But China's recent performance shows that its export growth has several sources.
Southeast Asia and Europe helped cover last year's American losses, while chips, machinery and electric vehicles are supporting further expansion.

articles.title_orig: China's DeepSeek, MiniMax win approval for AI global use, state media-affiliated entity says
articles.title_zh: China's DeepSeek, MiniMax win approval for AI global use, state media-affiliated entity says
articles.content_orig:
CCTV says the proposed measures are intended to establish clearer regulatory boundaries rather than shut the door on Chinese AI tech exports
Chinese artificial intelligence model developers DeepSeek and MiniMax have completed export registration procedures and proceeded with open-source releases and overseas licensing activities, according to Chinese state media, days after Beijing moved to tighten oversight on AI tech transfers.
The draft proposal released by the Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) and Ministry of Science and Technology, which also included provisions that came into immediate effect requiring official registration for the covered technologies, raised questions about whether Beijing was restricting Chinese AI companies from expanding overseas, particularly as the country’s open-weight models have gained international adoption.

articles.title_orig: Powerful earthquake in Tibet kills at least 16 people
articles.title_zh: Powerful earthquake in Tibet kills at least 16 people
articles.content_orig:
Watch: CCTV vision shows moment quake strikes in Tibet
A magnitude 7.0 earthquake has hit a mountainous region in Tibet, killing at least 16 people and injuring dozens, according to Chinese state media.
The centre of the quake hit BaqÃªn County in the Nagqu region on Thursday night, Xinhua reported, citing the local emergency management bureau.
The county - located in what China calls the Tibet Autonomous Region after annexing it in the 1950s - is 400km (250 miles) north-east of the region's capital, Lhasa.
Authorities have declared the incident an emergency and deployed rescue teams to the affected area, where 65 others have been injured, including 11 people with severe injuries.
The electricity supply has been cut off and 339 homes have collapsed in the affected region, though by Friday morning there were reports of power restored in some areas.
Local media said more than 12,400 people had been relocated following the earthquake.
Rockfall has forced roads in the region to close, making it more difficult for crews to reach impacted high-altitude areas.
The US Geological Survey (USGS) has recorded seven tremors close to the epicentre, all of which are located in the mountainous region. The largest tremor was recorded at 5.2 magnitude at a depth of 10km.
Shallow earthquakes and tremors closer to the Earth's surface are more damaging than deep quakes.
Rescuers search through rubble after Tibet earthquake
Several survivors of the earthquake have told local media about their harrowing escape.
Nagqu resident Yixi Cuomu told Tibet Daily that she was asleep in her bed when her house started shaking violently. Realising it was an earthquake, she headed outside barefoot, her "legs trembling uncontrollably" as she descended the staircase in her home.
Another eyewitness said the shaking was so violent "that in that moment I felt as if several hundred yaks were running past us".
Residents chose to spend the night outdoors in subzero temperatures, seeking shelter in tents or their cars, as they feared aftershocks could trap them in their homes, according to the news outlet.
Chinese state media reported on Friday morning that more than 400 aftershocks had been registered since the quake occurred.
China's Premier Li Qiang has called for "urgent efforts" to organise rescue operations and medical treatment for the injured, and relocate and resettle affected residents appropriately, according to state media.
Li noted that the earthquake-hit area is at a high altitude, around 4,800m (15,750ft), and prone to aftershocks.
The Ministry of Emergency Management has dispatched a working group to the affected area to guide rescue and disaster relief operations.
Separately, the Chinese government announced it was allocating 50 million yuan (Â£5.6m; $7.5m) for disaster relief efforts in Tibet.
Firefighters are seen helping residents injured by the quake in BaqÃªn, Tibet
Videos on social media of the moment the quake struck show villagers running into the streets as buildings shake violently in the dark. These have not been independently verified.
The region is prone to devastating seismic activity.
In 2023, a 6.2 magnitude quake killed more than 120 people in the nearby mountainous Gansu province of China.
Tibet and Nepal were also recently devastated by massive floods and landslides less than two months ago, unleashed by a glacier collapse, which killed at least 1,400 people. Hundreds of others are still reported missing.
Despite the region presenting some of the most challenging rescue conditions, rescue teams on the Tibetan plateau are highly experienced and have shown an ability to mobilise quickly.
In January 2025, military personnel, firefighters, police and specialist rescue teams were in the area within hours after a powerful eartquake struck the Shigatse region of Tibet.
The Chinese military also have drones to help survey the area.
Tibet, which has long demanded greater autonomy, is one of the most tightly controlled regions in China.
With foreign media restricted from the region and information heavily censored by authorities, Chinese state media is the main source for updates and details when such disasters happen.

articles.title_orig: Uzbekistan strengthens its relations with China and US
articles.title_zh: Uzbekistan strengthens its relations with China and US
articles.content_orig:
In recent days, Uzbekistan welcomed the Chinese and American governments in quick succession.
During Chinese Premier Li Qiang’s visit on 17-18 October, the Uzbek presidential administration said that joint projects backed by firm agreements had reached nearly $60 billion.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio then arrived in Samarkand for C5+1 talks, accompanied at the time by American business leaders seeking contracts, particularly in critical minerals. During the visit, Uzbekistan announced 54 agreements covering trade, investment, and technology. The agreements are said to be worth a total of $12 billion, according to Uzbekistan’s Ministry of Investment, Industry and Trade. However, China still accounts for 23% of Uzbekistan’s foreign trade in January-August 2026, while US goods trade with Uzbekistan totalled at $1.05 billion in 2025, which is less than a fifteenth of the value of its trade with China. Rubio said Washington was not asking Central Asian countries to stop cooperating with other partners, but would instead compete for investment.
Tashkent is likely to welcome investment from both sides, but the trade gap shows how challenging it will be if it were to decrease its dependence on Beijing.
“Chinese Premier Li Qiang visited Uzbekistan on October 17–18, just ahead of United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who arrived in Samarkand on October 18 with a delegation of American business leaders seeking new contracts.
While China already has a substantial presence in Uzbek manufacturing and energy, Washington is seeking to expand American involvement in critical minerals and technology. The visits highlight the growing competition between the world’s two largest economies for influence in Central Asia.
On October 17, President Shavkat Mirziyoyev received Li Qiang. According to the Uzbek presidential administration, the portfolio of joint projects backed by firm agreements has reached nearly $60 billion. More than 6,000 joint ventures with Chinese participation have been established in Uzbekistan. (...) Construction of the China–Kyrgyzstan–Uzbekistan railway was another topic of discussion. Work officially began in December 2024. The route will cross mountainous areas of Kyrgyzstan and connect the railway networks of China and Uzbekistan. The 304-kilometer section through Kyrgyzstan alone is estimated to cost $4.7 billion and will require 50 bridges and 29 tunnels. (...)
On October 19, Rubio attended talks in Samarkand under the C5+1 format, bringing together the U.S. and Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan. Rubio said nearly 300 American businesses were represented in Samarkand. Companies were discussing agreements potentially worth billions of dollars, with concrete announcements expected following the meetings. Among Washington’s priorities are critical minerals used in advanced technologies, including electronics and batteries.”
source: Caucasus and Central Asia Concise Vol 1 No 6 with Times of Central Asia

articles.title_orig: Winter arrives in markets
articles.title_zh: Winter arrives in markets
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
(Bloomberg) -- US Treasuries are showing tentative signs of reclaiming their traditional role as a haven — threatening to wrong-foot investors who are heavily positioned for this year's bond slump to deepen.
White House Turmoil Erupts as Trump Axes Zacharia, Backs Wiles
Ambani Taps Massive Reliance Workforce to Boost Jio's Record IPO
Trump Faces Midterm Fuel Reckoning as Gas Prices Near Biden's Average
Canadian Military Base Fire Kills Seven People, CBC Says
Judge Threatens Trump With Sanctions to Testify in BBC Lawsuit
As concerns mount across markets over the outlook for leading artificial-intelligence firms and the potential impact on the broader economy, 10-year yields fell about 17 basis points last week while the Nasdaq 100 Index tumbled 5.5%.
The previous time yields and the tech benchmark dropped that much in the same week was during the April 2025 tariff turmoil.
The bond rally was notable after months when Treasuries largely failed to provide their customary protection during periods when stocks were struggling. Hot inflation, a resilient economy and a flood of government and corporate borrowing — including to finance the AI boom — combined to push 10-year US yields up the past seven months, to their highest levels in more than two decades.
The latest wobble in stocks upset that trend in part because investors were sitting on unusually aggressive bearish Treasuries bets, raising the prospect of short-covering and heightening the two-way risk in the bond market even as inflation stays solid.
"To paraphrase Mark Twain, rumors of the death of US Treasuries are greatly exaggerated," said James Athey, a portfolio manager at Marlborough Investment Management.
Of course, it's tough to conclude that the AI boom, which has added trillions of dollars to stock-market valuations, is coming to an end. Previous bouts of volatility have proved short-lived.
But concerns over signs of slowing revenue growth at Anthropic PBC and the sinking debt prices of AI cloud-computing provider CoreWeave Inc. are raising questions about whether cracks are emerging in a trade that helped drive the bond rout. Massive AI investment has boosted the economy, while surging demand for computer chips added to inflationary pressures.
"An AI-led downturn would be a lot closer to a more traditional negative demand shock" and a catalyst for disinflation, Afonso Borges, a fixed-income strategist at Julius Baer, wrote in a report. In that kind of episode, he said, "intermediate Treasuries should again serve as an effective portfolio hedge."
Against that backdrop, the firm recommends an overweight duration stance in the intermediate area. Borges pointed out that 10-year Treasuries consistently delivered positive returns during equity drawdowns between 2000 and 2020.
The deluge of corporate issuance to finance AI infrastructure has increased competition for capital, another headwind for Treasuries. If expectations for AI investment fade, those forces could begin to work in reverse. Investment-grade companies – led by megacap tech firms — have sold about $1.7 trillion of bonds this year, up some 29% from this time last year.
"If investors are seeing their AI-linked bonds losing value, they will be less interested in buying new bonds," said John Briggs, head of US rates strategy at Natixis North America. "So that's taken an arrow out of the AI issuance quiver in the short term, and the result is more buying of the Treasury long end as there's less worry around crowding out."
Trader positioning could also amplify the bond strength if the AI trade extends its weakness. The gains in Treasuries drew fuel from investors known as commodity trading advisers exiting bearish futures positions, after they entered last week at extremely short levels.
The haven flows helped relieve pressure on bonds from persistent inflation. Hotter-than-expected consumer-price figures last week initially prompted traders to boost bets the Federal Reserve will lift interest rates this month, pushing the probability to about 50% at one point.
But as the stock selloff intensified, the perceived chances of an October hike diminished. They dwindled further after Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh, appearing at the International Monetary Fund's annual meetings, made no remarks on monetary policy or his economic outlook, apart from reiterating that the Fed will deliver price stability.
Traders still see the central bank tightening once by year-end and again in 2027. Given those expectations, Standard Bank's Steven Barrow called the recent bond rally a "red herring." The firm's head of G-10 strategy pointed to the inflation risk ahead and a structural trend toward equity ownership and away from sovereign bonds.
A Friday surge in oil prices, which have soared amid the Iran war and fanned inflation concerns, also showed how easily bonds' role as a hedging instrument can be upended. Both Treasuries and stocks weakened in parallel around midday as crude jumped amid doubts about President Donald Trump's deal to release more Russian diesel into global markets.
Looking forward, the uncertainty stemming from the lack of forward guidance coming from the Warsh — a core principle of his monetary-policy approach — leaves the market more vulnerable to large price swings, said Masahiko Loo, a Tokyo-based senior fixed-income strategist at State Street Investment Management.
However, for longer-term investors, "the picture looks different," Loo said. "If we get a bigger AI-driven risk-off episode, Treasuries increasingly appear capable of providing the hedge investors have been missing for much of the last few years."

articles.title_orig: Hundreds of flights cancelled across East Asia as Typhoon Champi roars toward Taiwan
articles.title_zh: Hundreds of flights cancelled across East Asia as Typhoon Champi roars toward Taiwan
articles.content_orig:
Taiwan is bracing for powerful Typhoon Champi, which is passing close to the island's east coast with torrential rains and gusts of up to 191 kph (119mph)
Taiwanese authorities have urged people to stay away from coasts and mountains, and are evacuating residents on the north-east coast living near a landslide dam at risk of breaching in the storm
Hundreds of flights in Taiwan and neighbouring Japan have been cancelled , affecting thousands of passengers
At least one person has died in Taiwan after being swept away by waves, according to authorities
Champi is the latest in a string of intense typhoons as a Super El NiÃ±o heats up the Pacific Ocean and fuels storms
Edited by Joel Guinto, with reporting from Joyce Lee in Taipei, Benny Lu in Hong Kong, Kurumi Mori in Tokyo and Koh Ewe in Singapore
Benny Lu BBC Chinese, reporting from Hong Kong
Taiwan's Central Weather Administration continues to issue warnings for both sea and land as Typhoon Champi approaches.
Champi is currently located southeast of Yilan, moving northwest and then northeast. Its storm circle is gradually enveloping Taiwan, posing a threat to the country and outlying islands such as Penghu.
The Central Weather Bureau says Champi is expected to slow down as it moves towards the north-east coast from this afternoon to evening, and may even exhibit irregular movements such as circling.
Therefore, the current assessment is that the chance of it making landfall is not high.
Rainfall is expected to be most significant tomorrow morning, and the storm will move away from the island by tomorrow night.
Typhoons get their names from a list compiled by the World Meteorological Organization, an agency of the UN.
The names are submitted by member countries.
Some, like Dolphin, are in English. Some are in the local language, like Chan-hom (a Laotian tree), Peilou (a migratory bird in Macau) and Nangka (the Malay name for jackfruit).
Countries like the Philippines give typhoons their own local names because of the sheer number of storms that affect the country every year.
Filipino meteorologists are referring to Typhoon Champi as Rosal - the local name for the gardenia plant.
Typhoon names can be recycled for different storms, but are usually retired after they cause serious destruction, like Typhoon Haiyan (or Yolanda in the Philippines), which killed more than 6,000 people in 2013; or Typhoon Fung-wong ( Uwan in the Philippines), which killed dozens when it struck the Philippines and Taiwan last November.
We can now bring you more pictures from Keelung, a major port city in north-eastern Taiwan.
Residents have been warned by Taiwan's Central Weather Bureau to expect "torrential or extremely torrential rain" in the city.
Earlier we reported that this has been an unusually hectic typhoon season for the region .
But it's not just typhoons. Recent months have seen a range of extreme weather events around the world.
Much of this is because of an exceptionally strong El NiÃ±o - a naturally occurring event that happens once every few years and lasts for around a year.
During this period, trade winds in the Pacific Ocean can weaken or reverse, allowing warm water to spread eastwards.
The heat from the ocean lifts global temperatures and changes rainfall patterns.
The UK Met Office said this is shaping up to be the "largest El NiÃ±o in living memory". This means 2027 is likely going to be the world's hottest year on record, the agency said.
Weather forecasters may be unsure if Champi will make landfall in Taiwan, but the hazards from the storm, one of the strongest on the planet this year, remain.
Taiwan's weather agency forecasts that up to 90cm (35in) will fall from Thursday to Saturday, with the north-east coast expected to be the hardest-hit.
"People should be aware that the strong winds and extremely heavy rain will continue into the first half of tomorrow (Saturday)," Central Weather Administration administrator Lu Kuo-chen says.
A typhoon has technically made landfall when its centre or eye moves from the sea onto land, according to Taiwan's weather agency.
Across the Asia region, however, many typhoons have caused widespread damage even when the eye has not made landfall.
Storms that skirt coastlines are capable of stirring torrential rains and strong winds that cause floods and landslides.
We reported earlier that Taiwanese authorities were warning people to stay alert as the island braced for Typhoon Champi to make landfall.
But for now, it remains unclear if the storm will make landfall in Taiwan or just brush past the island's coast as it heads northwards to Japan.
Forecasts by the meteorological agencies in Taiwan and Japan show that the eye of the storm is expected to skirt past Taiwan's northeastern tip without making landfall.
But a forecaster from Taiwan's Central Weather Administration also told Reuters that they could not rule out landfall, if the storm "stalls, loops, or wobbles from side to side" as it approaches Taiwan.
As Champi moves closer to Taiwan, it is also stirring heavy rains and strong winds in Batanes, a Philippine island chain located between southern Taiwan and Luzon, the Philippines' main northern island.
The second-highest in a five-step wind warning system has been raised in the Batanes islands. This means 150km/h winds are expected.
Photos posted on the local government's Facebook page showed waves crashing into seaside villages and roads closed to traffic. There were no immediate reports of casualties.
While it is affected by many of the 20 or so tropical storms in the Philippines every year, communities in Batanes are reputed to be more resilient against inclement weather. Many homes are made of thick limestone, engineered to withstand typhoon winds.
Champi has hovered in waters north-east of the Philippines for days. It is known locally as Typhoon Rosal.
A few days ago, Typhoon Champi officially became the strongest storm of the year.
On Tuesday afternoon, it attained a maximum sustained wind speed of 185mph (298km/h) as it moved over the Philippine sea  - the equivalent of a Category 5 hurricane.
Typhoon Champi was initially categorised as a "super typhoon", which is when a cyclone's sustained wind speed reaches 240 km/h(150 mph).
The typhoon appeared to weaken on Wednesday as it continued travelling through the sea.
But it remains powerful, carrying sustained winds of 155km/h (96mph) near its centre around noon on Friday, according to Taiwan's weather authorities.
Kurumi Mori Tokyo correspondent
More than 160 flights have been cancelled across four Japanese airlines.
Japanese airline All Nippon Airways (ANA) just said all flights departing from and arriving at Miyako Airport and Ishigaki Airport, in the southern Okinawa prefecture, are canceled for the entire day.
It also says operations being impacted at Okhotsk Monbetsu, Okinawa Naha Airport, Tsushima, Miyazaki, and Kagoshima Airports.
In an update moments ago, Japan Airlines said it had cancelled flights to Taipei Songshan Airport and Taiwan Taoyuan International Airport.
Kurumi Mori Tokyo correspondent
Here in Japan, 3,630 households are experiencing power outages due to the impact of the typhoon, according to Okinawa Electric Power.
The company says the strong rain and wind are creating dangerous conditions for outdoor work, so theyâre conducting restoration work via remote operation.
Iâm in Tokyo, where itâs just cloudy, but forecasts call for four straight rainy days starting tomorrow.
Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has warned people to remain alert to the typhoon, telling them to "exercise extreme caution against storm-force winds, high waves, sediment disasters and storm surges through tomorrow".
"Vigilance is also needed against flooding in low-lying areas, as well as rising and overflowing rivers" in the Okinawa and Amami regions, she wrote in a post on X.
Many have replied to Takaichi's post, thanking her for keeping them updated on social media as fewer people are watching TV or reading newspap

articles.title_orig: Japan to simulate cyberattacks as PHP flaws roil global internet
articles.title_zh: Japan to simulate cyberattacks as PHP flaws roil global internet
articles.content_orig:
Wiz Research uncovered multiple critical vulnerabilities in core PHP, a popular general-purpose scripting language that powers 70% of all websites in the world. Successful exploitation could allow attackers to take control of affected servers, steal sensitive data, and deface the websites running on them.
PHP is a backbone of the web: it’s the programming language powering WordPress, Joomla, Drupal, Wikipedia’s MediaWiki, and many others.
These vulnerabilities include memory disclosure and unauthenticated remote code execution in PHP itself, independent of the application running on top of it , putting every affected website in immediate risk.
Every PHP version released in the last decade is affected by at least one of these vulnerabilities, going back to version 5.4. Attackers can exploit them remotely, in some cases fairly easily. Immediate patching is strongly advised.
On October 21, 2026, PHP released the patch fixing multiple memory-safety vulnerabilities in the core engine.
These findings rank among the most severe vulnerabilities discovered in PHP, and arguably in software history. The underlying flaws had been present for decades, but demonstrating their exploitability  required an exceptionally complex chain of steps, at the edge of what human researchers could practically achieve. Frontier AI models substantially reduced that barrier, turning a longstanding flaw into an exploit.
In this post, we explain how frontier AI helped us find and fix vulnerabilities that had remained hidden in the PHP codebase for more than a decade. The issues described below all stem from key architecture decisions, some made over a decade ago, and were grouped under two CVEs, with severity reaching CVSS 9.2. The work grew into a cross-industry effort to protect customers, find variants, deploy detections and mitigations, and verify a patch in time for coordinated disclosure.
Nearly every PHP version is affected by at least one of these issues, including releases dating back to PHP 5.4. The vulnerabilities can allow unauthenticated attackers to execute code on affected servers or read sensitive process memory. That memory may contain passwords, authentication tokens, API keys and certificates belonging to other requests or the server itself.
PHP is the programming language behind much of the web, powering WordPress, Drupal and MediaWiki, the software that runs Wikipedia. A flaw in its core engine can affect websites across this ecosystem, even when their own application code is secure.
Some vulnerabilities become turning points because they challenge fundamental assumptions about security. In 2014, Heartbleed exposed the fragility of shared infrastructure securing the internet. In 2021, Log4Shell revealed how deeply embedded software dependencies could create widespread exposure that organizations struggled to identify. We believe PHP2Shell could mark a similar turning point for the AI era, illustrating how AI can change the practical exploitability of longstanding vulnerabilities. Building the exploit required chaining multiple flaws and adapting to each target’s memory layout through repeated testing and debugging. Frontier models were critical to making this process practical, enabling us to develop and adapt working exploits across multiple applications in hours. As the time and expertise required for this work decrease, complexity may no longer provide a meaningful barrier, changing how we define what is vulnerable in practice.
Wiz Research would like to thank the PHP team, Calif and OpenAI for their work on discovery, coordination and patch verification. OpenAI and Calif also published blogs containing details on the vulnerability – its history, technical details, and insight into the disclosure process. PHP posted as well.
We’d also like to express our sincere gratitude towards Automattic, Akamai, AWS, Cloudflare , Fastly , Google , Imperva, Microsoft, Vercel , and many others, for helping prepare guidance and out-of-the-box mitigations for customers who cannot apply the patch immediately.
All of the disclosed vulnerabilities are memory-safety issues that stem from bugs in how PHP handles fatal errors while processing requests, particularly out-of-memory errors. These bugs can leave a corrupted internal PHP state behind after a request ends unexpectedly. A later request or worker can reuse that stale state, leading to memory disclosure or corruption.
Below you can find a table that demonstrates what type of impact was demonstrated by each of the bugs we reported to PHP. The applications listed below are targets we chose for the RCE demonstrations. They are representative targets - exploitation does not require one of these CMSs, as the vulnerable code is in PHP itself.
Upload-progress unserializer use-after-free
Remote process-memory disclosure
Corrupt process memory and execute code
Unauthenticated disclosure of PHP worker memory
Pre-authentication RCE on WordPress, Drupal and Joomla
Application-agnostic remote memory disclosure
Fatal-error backtrace use-after-free
Corrupt process memory and execute code
Corrupt shared PHP state and execute code
Pre-authentication RCE on Drupal
Pre-authentication RCE on WordPress
While this blog covers only four instances of exploitable bugs (grouped under two CVEs) that follow this problematic pattern, there are other tracked, and likely untracked, variants of this issue in the PHP codebase. These variants have different requirements for exploitation and can lead to different types of impact. In any case, the patch provided by the PHP team fixes the issue at its core and eliminates all variants in the patched release.
We combined these vulnerabilities into a single exploit script, php2shell, and demonstrated that it could execute code remotely without authentication on deployments of WordPress ( wordpress:latest ), Drupal ( drupal:latest ), and Joomla ( joomla:latest ), using their latest container images at the time of testing.
These platforms illustrate the impact, but the vulnerabilities are in PHP itself. Exploitation does not depend on a flaw in the application’s code: even a simple “Hello World” application running on an affected PHP version can be vulnerable.
Separately, we demonstrated that attackers could read sensitive data from the PHP process’s memory, including passwords, tokens, and API keys, without needing to achieve remote code execution.
Demonstrations of PHP2Shell with Wordpress, Joomla, and Drupal:
The vulnerable code had been present for more than a decade. Turning these flaws into working exploits required chaining multiple bugs and accounting for how PHP allocates and reuses memory across requests. Memory bugs are notoriously complex; differences in PHP versions, configurations and application behavior can break assumptions the exploit depends on. An attack that works against one deployment may need substantial adjustments to work against another, each requiring further analysis, testing and debugging. Pre-AI, this manual work would be difficult to implement and even harder to scale.
With AI this is no longer a barrier. LLMs can help adapt an exploit to different PHP versions, configurations and memory layouts. With testing and debugging tools, models can analyze failures and iterate on adjustments, reducing the specialist effort required for each target. This significantly lowers the barrier to scaling attacks across different deployments.
This changes the economics of both discovery and exploitation. As AI reduces the effort needed to develop and adapt complex exploits, vulnerabilities that once seemed impractical to exploit become viable targets.
We used Wiz Atlas , Gemini 4 Argon and GPT-5.6 Sol throughout this research. Notably, Gemini 4 Argon made an invaluable contribution to finding the vulnerability, exploit development, attack detection, and validation of the patch.

articles.title_orig: Global tech sell-off sparks flight to safety
articles.title_zh: Global tech sell-off sparks flight to safety
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Global equity markets mostly sank Thursday as tech firms resumed their downward spiral following a mixed bag of earnings from Wall Street titans, while sentiment was also soured by rising oil prices.
AI-linked companies continued their rollercoaster ride since hitting record highs in June amid worries over colossal investment sums and their timeline for profitability, with growing debt-servicing costs adding to the uncertainty.
On Wednesday, a blockbuster quarterly report from Elon Musk's SpaceX -- its second since listing in June -- provided what some hoped would be solid support leading into a crucial earnings season, lifting all three main Wall Street indexes.
But mixed after-hours releases from Meta and Tesla muddied the waters again for investors.
"Risk-off sentiment is returning amid high geopolitical tensions and a swirl of worries about financing the AI juggernaut," noted Susannah Streeter, chief investment strategist at Wealth Club.
Rising oil prices also dragged on markets, with Brent futures gaining four percent to $113.17 per barrel as Iran's Revolutionary Guards threatened to strike American bases across the Middle East if the US military continues to escort ships through the Strait of Hormuz.
Most of the biggest AI players still haven't reported results yet, but markets were not thrilled with reports released late Wednesday.
Electric vehicle-maker Tesla announced lower profits in July-September and cut its capital spending forecast for this year, while Facebook-parent Meta lifted its estimates for how much it would spend on artificial intelligence.
Shares in Tesla shed 3.1 percent in New York, while those in Meta slumped 7.0 percent.
Wall Street's main indices moved lower, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite dropping 2.6 percent.
Briefing.com analyst Patrick O'Hare cited Meta's spending plans as a catalyst, along with a cautious outlook from Lam Research citing supply chain constraints as a problem.
Such dynamics suggest "companies won't be able to grow as much as has been afforded in their stock trade," said O'Hare, who pointed to strong demand for US Treasuries as evidence investors are seeking low-risk investments.
"Investors are seeking some safety under the theory that perhaps this AI trade could get unruly," he said.
Microsoft, Amazon and Alphabet are due to report next week, with Apple and Nvidia up in November.
Asian tech stocks sank Thursday, dragging broader markets with them, with South Korean chipmakers SK hynix and Samsung down 5.5 percent and four percent respectively.
Japan's Kioxia and Tokyo Electron were off as much as seven percent.
The Kospi index in Seoul fell more than three percent and Tokyo's Nikkei 225 was off 2.7 percent.
Hong Kong slid more than three percent, with NetEase and Tencent taking a battering, while Chinese e-commerce giants Alibaba and JD.com were also weighed by government calls for tighter quality standards.
European stock markets, which feature far fewer major tech firms, ended the day lower.
The Paris CAC 40 shed 1.4 percent amid concerns over high government debt in France and the recent violent street protests across the country.
Heading losses on the Paris stock market was Hermes -- its share price down 4.9 percent after the luxury fashion brand reported quarterly sales that undershot market expectations.

articles.title_orig: UnitedHealthcare, Humana Medicare Advantage cancellations to affect 1M
articles.title_zh: UnitedHealthcare, Humana Medicare Advantage cancellations to affect 1M
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Medicare open enrollment is here once again, and millions of older Americans are weighing the changes coming to their plans — and whether their insurer can still offer the coverage they need.
While beneficiaries consider whether to stick with their current advantage plan, find a new one or switch to traditional care, a KFF analysis shows Medicare Advantage options have dropped to just 35 plans in 2027 , down from 39 in 2026. About 1% of enrollees will lose their Medicare Advantage prescription drug plan as a result of this broader decrease in selection.
Dave Ramsey warns nearly 50% of Americans are making 1 big Social Security mistake. Here's what it is and 3 simple steps to fix it ASAP
The tax breaks in Trump's 'big beautiful bill' expire after 2028. Here are 4 reasons why retirees can't afford to waste time
Jeff Bezos backs a platform that lets anyone invest in rental homes for as little as $100 — 6 ways to build wealth like a landlord without actually being one
On top of that, Part D subsidies are expiring at the end of this year, which are in place to cap the premiums seniors pay for prescription drug plans. About half of plan recipients will likely be faced with a higher cost of care as a result, an administration official told ABC News.
That's a lot to consider ahead of the Dec. 7 enrollment deadline. And it could be why comedian John Oliver and personal finance expert Suze Orman have long since made arguments against Medicare Advantage (MA).
But here's how to make your own call.
Last year, "Last Week Tonight" host John Oliver devoted a critical 31-minute segment to MA , arguing that the program is "woefully insufficient," riddled with denials and delays, and costly to taxpayers.
Oliver accused major insurers of inflating patient risk scores to drive up federal payments and using restrictive networks and prior authorizations to limit care.
"When you take all this together, you get a system where the incentives are clearly set up for insurance companies to make you look as sick as possible on paper, while doing as little as possible to help you when you actually need it," he summarized.
Personal finance expert Suze Orman has also been criticizing MA. In a widely shared post , she argued that original Medicare is "better" and warned that major insurers — including UnitedHealthcare and Humana — were going to terminate or consolidate plans for 2026, leaving older adults vulnerable to unexpected changes in premiums, networks and benefits.
Orman urged MA enrollees to carefully review their annual notice of change and consider switching back to traditional Medicare while they still can.
Read More: Vanguard reveals what's coming for U.S. stocks — and it's raising alarm bells for older investors
Despite the backlash, some MA users insist the plans work well for them because of their financial costs.
"I've had MA for eight years, and I've never spent more than $200 or $300 in a given year on copays," one Reddit user wrote .
Another said John Oliver "could harm a lot of folks" by implying MA is universally bad. These users argue that while MA has flaws, it remains the only affordable route for many.
On LinkedIn, former CVS Health and UnitedHealth executive Adam Korn questioned Oliver's criticism.
Two-thirds of customers are satisfied with their coverage — whether MA or traditional Medicare.
MA includes annual out-of-pocket caps, which Original Medicare does not.
MA plans offer supplemental benefits such as dental, vision, hearing, transportation and meal delivery support.
For many low-income or chronically ill seniors, MA provides more comprehensive support than the traditional program.
Over 66 million Americans rely on Medicare, and over 35 million are enrolled in Medicare Advantage.
Private insurers offer Medicare Advantage (Part C) and typically bundle hospital, medical and drug coverage, plus extras. It limits doctors to a network —and going out-of-network can be costly — but it caps annual out-of-pocket expenses .
Nearly all doctors accept original Medicare. But it:
covers only 80% of most medical (Part B) costs.
offers no out-of-pocket maximum.
often requires older adults to buy Medigap and Part D plans to avoid steep bills.
You can switch from MA to traditional Medicare during open enrollment, which runs until December 7.
If you do switch, you may also need to purchase a Medigap policy.
There is no one-size-fits-all answer.
Your plan covers your doctors.
Your medications are affordable.
You rarely need expensive care.
You value dental/vision/hearing benefits.
You cannot afford Medigap premiums.
Consider switching to original Medicare if:
You have a complex or chronic medical condition.
You want national provider flexibility.
You worry about MA plan terminations.
Prior authorizations have disrupted your care.
Millions of older adults rely on MA because it better fits their budgets and health needs. If you're confused about your options, consult a licensed insurance broker, a financial advisor or a counsellor at your state's State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP).

articles.title_orig: A Cancer Revolution
articles.title_zh: A Cancer Revolution
articles.content_orig:
Pope Leo XIV’s lung cancer surgery last week was a success, and no further treatment is required, the Vatican press office said in a bulletin Wednesday.
“The final histological reports and molecular biology analyses of the tissue removed during the Holy Father’s surgery have been completed today,” said Dr. Luigi Carbone, the pope’s personal physician, and Dr. Stefano Margaritora, a thoracic surgery professor who led the surgical team.
“The results have confirmed that the condition was a pulmonary adenocarcinoma and that the disease was localized. A subsequent oncological evaluation has confirmed that no further therapy is required,” the bulletin added.
Pulmonary adenocarcinoma is the most common type of lung cancer, accounting for roughly 40% of all cases. It’s slow-moving and often affects nonsmokers.
Leo’s announcement on October 11 that he required surgery for a “nodule” on his lung came as a shock both within and outside the Vatican, given the pope’s penchant for clean living. After a short stay at a hospital in Rome, where doctors removed the lobe of his right lung, Leo returned home on October 17.
The next day, he made his first public appearance since his diagnosis, leading the Sunday Angelus from the balcony of the Apostolic Palace.
“This experience has given me a profound sense of closeness to all those who are going through illness or a state of infirmity,” he told crowds of worshipers.
Pope Leo’s recovery has beeen much faster than normal, according to Dr. Juanita Mora, the national medical spokesperson for the American Lung Association, who was not part of his care team. She said doctors will monitor the pope after his recent treatment, including follow-up CT scans every three to six months for the first few years, then annually to check for any regrowth.
After such surgery, patients often have respiratory physiotherapy to restore breathing capacity, Mora told CNN, adding that his affected lung should regain full function.
The all-clear arrives ahead of the pontiff’s planned South America trip next month. The news that the pope had cancer complicated plans for the journey, scheduled to include stops in Peru, Uruguay and Argentina and require at least 14 flights.
Though the Vatican has not officially confirmed the pope’s plans for travel, Margaritora, his surgeon, told Vatican News that he saw “no clinical reasons” for canceling the trip.
If the trip goes ahead, the pontiff will probably be told to walk during his travels to prevent blood clots that can form during long flights, according to Mora. The pope, she said, should get Covid-19, flu and RSV vaccines ahead of his trip for “a little extra protection in case he were to get any of the respiratory infections.”
CNN’s Sharon Braithwaite and Jen Christensen contributed reporting.
This is a developing story and will be updated.

articles.title_orig: Heat killed ‘staggering’ 50,000 people in Europe’s cities this summer, scientists warn
articles.title_zh: Heat killed ‘staggering’ 50,000 people in Europe’s cities this summer, scientists warn
articles.content_orig:
People succumbed to heat at highest rates in Malta, Italy and Hungary, with health issues, loneliness and poverty exacerbating toll
Heat killed a record 50,000 people in European cities this summer, new research suggests, with scientists blaming climate breakdown for two in every three of the deaths.
Morgues and funeral homes filled with bodies from June to August as the heat added by planet-baking pollution cut short an extra 32,000 lives in urban areas, the researchers found. Hot days pushed vulnerable bodies into overdrive and warm nights prevented them from recovering.
The “staggering” death toll, modelled using historical relationships between heat and health in 854 cities, was the worst on record, the study found. Hot weather marked by relentless heatwaves killed nearly twice as many people as it did in each of the two next most dangerous years.
“In some sense, the absolute numbers of the heat-related deaths estimated across the 854 urban areas are indeed staggering,” said Malcolm Mistry, a climate and health scientist at the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine, who co-authored the study. “But perhaps what is even more alarming is the proportion of these deaths that we attribute to anthropogenic climate change.”
The share of deaths due to climate breakdown has risen from about 40% at the start of the century to 65% this summer, the study found.
People succumbed to heat at the highest rates in Malta, Italy and Hungary, while absolute death tolls were greatest in Italy, France, Spain, Germany and the UK. Because death certificates rarely record contributing factors – such as dangerous temperatures that push a stroke victim or lung cancer patient past their limits – families rarely know that heat and human activity hastened their relatives’ death.
“These shocking figures represent thousands of families who have lost a loved one this summer due to the climate crisis,” said Katie White, the climate transition minister for the UK, where scientists estimated 4,354 heat deaths this summer.”
In Naples, the hardest-hit city on the continent, 815 people per million died from the heat, according to the study’s age-standardised estimates. Mario Guarino, an emergency doctor at Ospedale CTO in the north of the city, said he witnessed a 15% increase in emergency room visits during the hottest weeks.
The “defining characteristic” of the period was the complexity of health problems exacerbated by heat, he added, with loneliness and poverty worsening the situation further.
“We took in a terminal cancer patient who lived in a hot attic simply because his family couldn’t find a company to install air conditioning during the summer,” said Guarino. “An elderly man with dementia was abruptly abandoned by his Ukrainian caregiver who returned home to say goodbye to her son, who had been called to war. Emergency services found [the man] lying on the floor one night with a fractured pelvis, desperately trying to call the tenant next door.”
The study found people over the age of 85 made up almost half of the death toll, though younger people were not immune, with 833 people between the age of 20 and 44 also thought to have died due to the heat. The scientists said the death toll from the cities studied, which account for about 40% of the European population, could not be easily extrapolated to estimate the full death toll including those in towns and villages.
after newsletter promotion
The scorching heat that persistently baked western Europe this summer was the worst on record, the EU’s climate monitoring service announced this month , with more than half the continent seared by “very strong” heat stress that felt hotter than 38C. Slightly less punishing temperatures in eastern Europe brought the continental average to its third-hottest level on record.
Greenhouse gases have warmed Europe about twice as fast as the global average, exposing more people to intolerably hot summers and fewer people to dangerously cold winters. While cold is a bigger killer than heat, scientists expect rising temperatures to claim more lives than they save, as heat deaths are projected to rise faster than cold deaths fall.
The study combined established relationships between heat and mortality with temperature data for 2026 to rapidly estimate the fallout from this summer’s heat. The death tolls for individual countries differ from what national public health agencies have calculated using their own methods.
David García-García, a researcher at the mortality monitoring system at the Carlos III health institute in Madrid, who was not involved in the study, said it was a “valuable contribution” that allowed for comparisons across the continent. “However, it is important to bear in mind that these are estimates based on observed temperatures and epidemiological models, which do not incorporate actual data on deaths occurring in the summer of 2026,” he said.
Doctors have urged governments to burn fewer fossil fuels – the core driver of rising temperatures – while bolstering health systems, greening cities, rolling out air conditioning and encouraging people to drink water and seek shade. They have also stressed the benefits of people checking in on vulnerable neighbours and family members so they can get help before tragedy strikes.
“The real epidemic these days is loneliness,” said Guarino. “Many elderly people are left alone during the summer, abandoned by their families, and due to their low income, they can’t afford air conditioning or, if they do have it, avoid turning it on because of the cost of electricity.”

articles.title_orig: At least 16 dead in Tibet quake, Chinese state media says
articles.title_zh: At least 16 dead in Tibet quake, Chinese state media says
articles.content_orig:
More than a dozen people were killed and hundreds of homes destroyed when a magnitude 7.0 earthquake hit China's Tibet region on Thursday evening local time, according to local officials.
The United States Geological Survey said the quake occurred at 10:33 p.m. local time, with its epicenter 119 miles east-northeast of Nagqu, in a sparsely populated, high-altitude area of northern Tibet.
At least 16 people were killed and 54 people were injured in the earthquake, Chinese state media said.
Search and rescue efforts continued following the collapse of at least 339 homes and 20 livestock sheds, the Nagqu media office said, citing city government officials. Among the injured, 11 people were in serious condition and the other 35 sustained minor injuries, the media office said.
More than 1,600 people from the local county were deployed for rescue efforts. Supplies including 1,000 prefabricated housing units, around 3,000 tents and folding beds, as well as flashlights and winter clothing arrived in the region.
It was the biggest earthquake in the region in the last five years, China's national broadcaster CCTV said.
Nagqu is more than 186 miles north of Tibet's capital, Lhasa.
The USGS put the earthquake's depth at 11 miles.  Xinhua, citing the China Earthquake Networks Center, put the depth at 6.2 miles.
The earthquake comes less than two months after a border region of Nepal and Tibet was struck by devastating flash flooding that left hundreds of people dead and destroyed several communities . Authorities said the flooding was caused by the collapse of a glacier.

articles.title_orig: Caught between the US and China
articles.title_zh: Caught between the US and China
articles.content_orig:
The Thai-flagged bulk carrier Mayuree Naree, which was struck by a missile near the Strait of Hormuz in February, is seen stranded off the coast of Qeshm Island, Iran, on Sept. 11, 2026
Iran may have found a weapon in the American electoral calendar. With the midterm elections two weeks away, Tehran is intensifying attacks on shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz, calculating that higher energy prices will deepen President Donald Trump’s political troubles and make another U.S. military campaign too costly to contemplate.
The wager is seductive: an American president anxious about diesel prices and his party’s prospects in the midterms, Iran seems to believe, will have little appetite for another major war.
Trump’s declaration that he will refrain from striking Iran before the Nov. 3 vote appears to vindicate this view, even as he periodically threatens to use force again. Having survived two rounds of war and absorbed punishing economic losses, Iran’s leaders believe they can endure a little longer. By disrupting Gulf commerce, they gain leverage their conventional forces cannot provide. They also hope to make that leverage permanent and compel Washington to accept Tehran’s authority over passage through the world’s most important energy chokepoint.
Yet the past nine months of war against Iran have made it clear that renewed military conflict before the midterms or after the elections is unlikely to resolve the disputes between the U.S. and Iran. The two countries will eventually have to sit across the negotiating table to resolve their long-running disputes.
Tehran may be misreading how political peril shapes an adversary’s decisions. Trump could decide that appearing powerless as Iranian attacks push up prices is more damaging than another round of military strikes. Reports that his administration has considered fresh strikes suggest the military option remains in play. A serious attack on American forces could turn Trump’s promise of restraint into a political liability overnight.
The political situation in Israel adds a combustible variable. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu faces an Oct. 27 election with his bloc struggling to secure a majority. He has staked his political reputation on the claim that only he can neutralize the Iranian threat.
With Tehran rebuilding its missile and drone capabilities and uncertainty surrounding its nuclear program, Netanyahu may see renewed strikes as both a strategic opportunity and a means of restoring his standing at home. Such a gamble could deepen Israel’s insecurity, but electoral desperation seldom improves anyone’s judgment.
The convergence of these calculations makes the coming weeks particularly perilous. Iran thinks Trump’s electoral weakness will constrain him. Trump and Netanyahu might each conclude that a show of force could rescue their political fortunes. Each side imagines it can calibrate the violence and manage the aftermath. The experience of this year’s conflict, in which successive rounds of fighting outran diplomatic efforts to contain them, offers little reason for that confidence.
Even if October passes without another conflagration, November brings its own hazards. After the midterm elections, the political constraints Trump has publicly imposed on himself will disappear. With substantial American forces already positioned in the region, Washington may be tempted to break the deadlock through another round of attacks. Tehran, fearing another surprise attack, might choose to strike Israel or U.S. military assets in the region first. What might seem like prudent preparation in Washington or Tehran could help bring about the war it is meant to deter.
The underlying impasse is as stubborn as ever. Washington wants a nuclear agreement and believes its blockade will ultimately compel Iran to negotiate. Tehran insists on upfront economic relief and an end to the war before substantive talks on the nuclear issue can begin.
America can point to tankers still transiting Hormuz, but shipping that depends on costly military protection and remains under threat is a poor substitute for normal trade. Iran can inflict considerable damage on the oil exports of its Gulf neighbors, but it has so far failed to turn that leverage into meaningful American concessions.
Another surge in hostilities would widen this gulf rather than bridge it. American and Israeli aircraft can destroy missile launchers, production facilities, and infrastructure, but Iran has repeatedly demonstrated that it can retaliate and survive. Iran’s response could extend further to target Gulf energy infrastructure, maritime commerce, data centers , and other critical networks.
The Houthi confrontation with Saudi Arabia already offers a grim illustration of how quickly the costs can spread. The war in Yemen has been reignited with devastating consequences, including deadly attacks on civilian airports and a spiraling cycle of retaliation. The fighting now threatens to draw in Turkey and Pakistan to support Saudi Arabia, as the three countries recently signed a mutual security pact known as the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement.
A new campaign could leave Iran poorer, Israel more exposed, and the U.S. burdened with an even more expensive regional commitment, while markets around the world absorb another shock.
The outlines of a diplomatic bargain have been visible for months: reciprocal steps to reopen Hormuz, calibrated sanctions relief, and a resumption of nuclear negotiations. The difficulty lies in sequencing and trust. Tehran fears that surrendering its maritime leverage first would invite fresh demands; Washington worries that easing pressure would reward coercion without securing lasting constraints on Iran’s nuclear program. Addressing those fears will require reciprocal steps and credible verification. More bombing won’t help.
Leaders contemplating an October surprise or an offensive after the midterms must remember that uncomfortable truth. Military force may alter the balance of pain without resolving the disputes each side will eventually have to confront across the negotiating table.
After another round of death and destruction, they could find themselves negotiating over the same issues, with less trust, greater bitterness, and far fewer resources to rebuild what they have broken. Their choices will be no easier then; the cost of reaching an agreement will be far greater.

articles.source: Institute for the Study of War
articles.content_orig:
Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment
The Kremlin’s seeming interest in negotiations aims not to end the war in Ukraine but rather to secure economic concessions from the United States such that Russia can continue funding its war. Various Russian officials tried to present the October 21 meeting between US Special Representative to the Middle East Steve Witkoff and Russian President Vladimir Putin as evidence that Russia is willing to engage in meaningful negotiations to end the war while simultaneously attempting to extract economic concessions from the United States so that Russia can continue funding the war.[1] Russian Direct Investment Fund (RDIF) CEO Kirill Dmitriev, for example, claimed on October 21 that Witkoff and Putin used the October 21 meeting to agree to expand Russian-US economic cooperation and to “continue communicating.”[2] A Kremlin domestic policy official told Russian opposition source Verstka that the Kremlin does not expect negotiations to resolve the war in Ukraine but that Russian officials hope to extract economic concessions, which could boost Russia’s budget and give Russia a military advantage.[3]
Other Russian officials meanwhile demonstrated Russia’s unwillingness to make any meaningful concessions toward ending the war in Ukraine. Kremlin Spokesperson Dmitry Peskov stated on October 22 that Putin did not present any Russian peace proposal to Witkoff during their meeting and that Putin has not considered the composition of a potential Russian delegation for a future Russia-US-Ukraine trilateral meeting.[4] Russian State Duma deputies expressed skepticism on October 21 and 22 that negotiations could end the war and reiterated claims that freezing the current frontlines would be detrimental to Russia’s own efforts to end the war.[5] A source close to the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) told Verstka on October 22 that the Kremlin has been working for over 1.5 years to try to sway the Trump administration to Russia’s side and that the Kremlin’s current negotiation efforts are emphasizing Ukraine’s alleged hopelessness. These are similar to the Kremlin’s earlier negotiation tactics which tried to convince the United States and the West generally that Ukrainian defenses were going to collapse such that Ukraine should preemptively capitulate.[6]
The Kremlin is fundamentally interested only in buying time to resolve the war on the battlefield while Russia simultaneously reaps the benefits of economic cooperation with the United States. State Duma Defense Committee First Deputy Chairperson Alexei Zhuravlyov stated on October 21 that Russia must “press” Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on the battlefield and force Ukraine to “capitulate.”[7] Zhuravlyov added that Russia should not rely on diplomacy with the United States because Russian “successes on the ground” will strengthen Russia’s negotiating position.[8] Russian Presidential Aide Yuriy Ushakov similarly claimed that Russian forces maintain the “complete strategic initiative” and are conducting a “relentless offensive” in all key areas of the frontline.[9]
Russian forces are not winning on the battlefield, however, particularly as Ukrainian forces have stymied the planned Russian offensive to seize Donetsk Oblast. ISW has observed evidence that Russian forces suffered a net loss of 241 square kilometers of territory in Ukraine since September 1, 2026. The average rate of daily Russian advances has significantly declined since 2025, with an average of 0.25 square kilometers per day so far in 2026. Ukrainian forces have, comparatively, been contesting and seizing the operational initiative across several sectors of the frontline throughout 2026, including most recently in the Lyman direction with Ukraine’s Operation Vivaldi which liberated over 270 square kilometers of territory and thwarted the Russian military command’s plan to encircle the Fortress Belt.[10] Russian forces are also facing mounting monthly casualties while the Russian recruitment rate continues to fall short of its loss rate.[11] Russian forces have suffered almost 37,000 casualties thus far in October 2026 — much higher than the 31,270 casualties for all of October 2025.[12] The Kremlin may face mounting challenges in the coming months, should Ukraine continue to contest the operational initiative and disrupt Russian offensive plans, potentially further pushing Russian commanders to urge Putin to conduct a mobilization in some form.[13]
The Kremlin is likely actively seeking economic cooperation with the United States as Russia faces significant financial strain. Sources familiar with the matter told Bloomberg on October 22 that even a few more months of continued war could exact lasting financial damage on Russian state-owned oil company Rosneft, as Ukrainian strikes against Rosneft’s oil refineries have significantly reduced the company’s profits and increased its debt.[14] Bloomberg added that repeated Ukrainian strikes have prevented Rosneft from completing repairs and restarting refinery operations and that strikes against complex secondary units that often include Western-sourced parts, like catalytic crackers, reformers, and hydrocrackers, are particularly difficult to repair. Russia remains highly susceptible to international sanctions that restrict its access to the technologically advanced components needed to repair the equipment damaged after Ukraine’s strikes.[15] The Kremlin is therefore pushing the United States for various forms of economic relief, so that Russia can continue funding its war against Ukraine.[16] The Kremlin has continuously sought to extract economic concessions during negotiations to alleviate the pressure on its oil industry — including restrictions on Ukrainian strikes against refineries and the relaxation of US sanctions against diesel exports — while expressing little real interest in ending the war.[17]
Russian forces conducted a massive missile and drone strike against Ukraine overnight on October 21 to 22 following the October 21 meeting between Witkoff and Putin — a continuation of Russia’s pattern of launching large strike packages in the days before and after major peace talks. The Ukrainian Air Force reported that Russian forces conducted a massive combined missile and drone strike primarily targeting Kyiv City and using an unspecified number of Iskander-M, S-400, Zircon, and Onyx missiles and 210 long-range drones, 110 of which were jet-powered.[18] Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that Russian forces conducted three waves of ballistic missile strikes against Kyiv City using 21 missiles, damaging residential, energy, railway, and commercial infrastructure.[19] Zelensky stated that Russian strikes targeted 12 Ukrainian oblasts, killing at least two people and injuring at least 34 people. Russian forces regularly conduct massive strikes in the days right before and after bilateral and trilateral talks, such as the August 2025 US-Russia Alaska summit, the November 2025 US-Ukraine talks in Geneva, the November 2025 US-Russia talks in Moscow, the December 2025 US-Ukrainian-European and US-Russian talks, and the January-February 2026 US-Ukrainian-Russian talks in Abu Dhabi.[20]
Russian forces struck Kyiv City with cluster munitions to purposely harm the civilian population, likely as part of wider Russian efforts to distract from Ukraine’s recent battlefield successes and ultimately force Ukraine into capitulation by making daily life untenable. Zelensky stated that Russian forces struck Pechersk Raion, the historic center of Kyiv City, with three ballistic missiles with cluster warheads that have a dispersion diameter of 400 meters.[21] The strikes damaged monastery buildings and other civilian infrastructure near the Kyiv Pechersk Lavra and the Holy Presentation Monastery. Zelensky noted that there were no military targets in the area and that the objective of the strikes was to cause widespread destruction.[22] Kyiv City Mayor Vita

articles.title_zh: Breakthrough vaccine for the deadliest skin cancer cut risk by almost half
articles.content_orig:
Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged in Please refresh your browser to be logged in
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.
A large clinical trial combining Moderna 's mRNA cancer vaccine with Merck 's immunotherapy reduced the risk of melanoma death or recurrence by 42%, the companies announced on Thursday, potentially opening a new era in personalized oncology.
Moderna shares closed more than 17% lower on Thursday after the trial findings leaked on an oncology website, despite having nearly quadrupled through Wednesday's close since August when the trial's success was first announced without full data. Merck stock also fell about 1.8%.
The Phase 3 trial, which tracked more than 1,100 patients, also revealed that the combination treatment reduced the risk of the cancer spreading by 38%.
The findings mark the first data demonstrating that pairing a custom vaccine based on a patient's unique tumor mutations with a drug that boosts the immune system can successfully halt the disease. The vaccine was tested alongside Merck's Keytruda, one of the world's top-selling medicines.
Keytruda functions by removing a natural brake that cancer cells rely on to hide from immune attack. Meanwhile, the vaccine instructs patient cells to produce copies of specific mutations, allowing the immune system to seek out and destroy them.
Moderna CEO Stephane Bancel stated that the findings herald a new chapter in treating cancer.
"With this ability to create new T cells that are specific to your tumor... the clinical impact is very profound, and as we saw in the Phase 2 (trial), very lasting," Bancel said in an interview.
The companies are preparing to file for US regulatory approval, expecting to launch the personalized cancer vaccine in 2027, Bancel noted.
The results, evaluating patient outcomes over the initial two years following treatment, are scheduled for presentation on Saturday at the European Society for Medical Oncology conference in Madrid.
Among subjects who received the vaccine paired with Keytruda, 82.2% remained cancer-free after two years, compared to 70% of those who received Keytruda alone.
"This is highly statistically significant. It is not by chance," said Dr. Hussein Tawbi, a melanoma expert and trial investigator at the University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center.
Ahead of the meeting, several Wall Street analysts noted that investors were looking for the combination to cut the risk of recurrence by 40% or more.
"There appears to be a sell-on-the-news reaction playing out here," William Blair analyst Myles Minter wrote in a research note, pointing out that Moderna shares remained up 525% this year even with Thursday's downward move.
Minter added that the findings were "great data, in our view, but investors will continue to debate the fundamental valuation."
The trial assessed nine doses of the vaccine, known as intismeran, administered with Keytruda beginning 13 weeks after surgery to remove melanoma lesions, comparing responses against the standard single-therapy treatment of Keytruda alone.

articles.title_orig: Injuries in China's Tibet rise to 65 after earthquake, death toll remains at 16
articles.title_zh: Injuries in China's Tibet rise to 65 after earthquake, death toll remains at 16
articles.content_orig:
At least 16 people have died and dozens were injured after a magnitude 7 earthquake struck Tibet on Thursday, according to Chinese state news agency Xinhua.
The epicenter was 183 kilometers East-Northeast of the city of Nagqu in the Tibet region, according to the United States Geological Survey.
At least 339 houses have collapsed and the extent of the damage is still being assessed, according to Xinhua. A rescue team has been dispatched to the epicenter.
Railway authorities have suspended train services through the affected areas, according to state media CCTV.
The China Earthquake Administration has activated a level II emergency response, its second-highest tier, Chinese broadcaster CGTN said.
In villages near the epicenter, authorities have found at least two injured people and houses with visible cracks, Reuters reported citing a state broadcaster.
Videos released by local media showed people leaving their homes as the quake struck, Reuters reported.
The average elevation within a 5-kilometer radius of the epicenter exceeds 4,800 meters, according to the China Earthquake Networks Center.
China is no stranger to powerful quakes, especially in southwestern parts of the country where the Eurasian tectonic plate meets the Indian plate, a dramatic collision that creates the mighty Himalayas and the vast Tibetan plateau.
Thursday’s earthquake comes roughly two months after the catastrophic flooding disaster on the edge of the Tibetan plateau on the border with Nepal, that was sparked by a huge glacier collapse and landslide. It killed at least 1,300 people and left more than 5,000 missing.
The last comparably-strong earthquake to rock China occurred in January 2024, when a 7.1-magnitude quake hit a mountainous and remote part of China’s far western Xinjiang region, killing three people and injuring scores more.
In December 2023, over one hundred people were killed when an earthquake hit China’s Jishishan county in Gansu province, northwest China, making it the country’s deadliest in nearly a decade.
This is a developing story and will be updated.
Michael Rios contributed to this report.
