articles.title_orig: A Typography Geek Pointed Out Something About The Space Shuttle Discovery And Now I Can't Unsee It
articles.title_zh: A Typography Geek Pointed Out Something About The Space Shuttle Discovery And Now I Can't Unsee It
articles.content_orig:
Even though I was born in the Apollo Era, barely, the spacecraft that I think had the most influence on my childhood had to be the Space Shuttles. I remember poring over diagrams and drawings of the shuttles in National Geographic foldouts, where they even took my attention from the Forbidden Nipples seen on some of the other pages. I remember watching that first launch of the shuttle Colombia in 1981, I remember the tragedy of the Challenger in 1986, and I remember covering the process of moving the orbiter Endeavour through the streets of Los Angeles to its eventual home at the California Science Center. And more recently, I’ve taken my kid to see the orbiter Discovery at the Udvar-Hazy Center just outside of Washington, DC.
It’s that orbiter that I want to talk about specifically, because I saw a social media post about the orbiter Discovery that grabbed my attention and held it with the sort of fierce grip I imagine Miss Piggy employs on Kermit’s impossibly thin limbs when they’re alone.
That post was on Threads, and I just figured out how to embed a post from that site, so here, you can see it for yourself:
Wait, what? Discovery has an upside-down ‘s’ in its name? How the hell did that happen? Discovery was usually considered, by astronauts and NASA people, the jewel in the Space Shuttle crown. It was recognized to be the most reliable and best-performing of all the orbiters, and had the most missions and time in space . Since it was first launched in 1984, Discovery completed 39 missions, spent in total a full year in space, and traveled 150 million miles.
The thing flew for 27 years, and somehow nobody noticed that the ‘s’ was upside down on the starboard side name text?
I mean, I guess I should be more understanding; I’ve seen it several times and never noticed, and it wasn’t until just tonight that I looked back at some old photos I took of Discovery the last time I was there and saw, holy crap, the dude on Threads was right. That ‘s’ is rotated 180°.
Now, the typography on the shuttle orbiters follows NASA’s carefully-planned and strictly-enforced graphic and typographic guidelines , which state that the typography used on the spacecraft should be Helvetica Medium:
Okay, let’s take a look at the typography on the orbiter:
(the ‘r’ on the font I used there feels a bit different, too, but this gets the point across and I have to get on a flight in a few hours so I’m gonna let that slide)
It’s a subtle difference, but as you can see, the starboard side’s name definitely has that flipped ‘s.’ It’s subtle, but the Helvetica ‘s’ is slightly wider on the bottom, giving the letter a somewhat more settled appearance. Here, look:
You can see the difference there, right? I feel like once it’s pointed out, you can’t help but notice it. The ‘v’ on the port side looks oddly thick, too, now that I’m looking at it.
I’ve been told that the graphics on these orbiters was applied using large stencils and special space-grade paint, and I’m sure the complex curves of the fuselage didn’t make the application of these elements easy. It’s understandable that a letter stencil may have been flipped around, but I am sort of surprised it was never corrected in its 27 years of service life.
All the other graphics and typography are applied with impressive precision; maybe there were people who knew that ‘s’ was wrong, but kind of liked that subtle imperfection, as it does add character to the spacecraft. I get that, absolutely. If I was in charge, I’d have just let it ride, too.
I still can’t believe I’d never clocked this before; as a typographic geek and a space geek who has spent far too much time looking at pictures of spacecraft in books and online, you’d think I’d have encountered this before, but, nope. Or if I did, it didn’t make enough of an impression to consciously note it or remember.
But now that it’s there? I can’t unsee it. And I’m sort of delighted by that.
I was in hazy years ago with some autist who discovered that about discovery and began ranting about it. I later heard a story about it from some air force space guys and some that have since turned space force guys echoed by a few others but don’t really remember the details. Something about they noticed at some point but just left it.
I still remember my dads aerospace engineer buddies after Challenger they knew it would do that because the temperature was too low and was out of spec for the seals. They called everyone they knew to get them to abort to no avail. They were messed up for a long time. They were working a primary defense contractor right outside of DC with some NASA contracts as well as lots of DOD contracts and contacts I always thought that was a bit strange.
Despite being a more recent than Challenger, the loss of Columbia is not so etched in my brain. I remember it happening, but not where I was at the time. My whole school watched Challenger blow up live, one of our teachers was a runner-up to Christa McAuliffe for Teacher in Space (and he was a cousin of mine to boot).
Being a graphic design obsessive is bad for your mental health. The little serifs on the circle around the current Nissan logo being perfectly parallel, so that they look as though they’re flaring slightly outwards, picks at my nits every time I see it. And, as if things weren’t bad enough, the horrible kerning of “USA” on DJ Trump’s baseball cap feels like a pointer to everything else that’s going wrong.
If his cap really reflected how bad everything was going, the font on it would be some horrid conglomeration of Papyrus and Comic Sans…
Bad kerning with a Times-style serif font shows real dedication to chaos.
It probably couldn’t be painted over without looking, you know…painted over. That leaves cutting it out, but that’s likely a whole section of ship, not just the patch the inverted S lives on. So live with it
I wonder if it was an *intentional* choice to do with the way the curvature of the body influences the perception of the lettering? The upper part of the ‘S’ being slightly further away from the viewer when seen from a right angle to the horizontal plane, which might make it appear smaller, making this the less visually odd of the two choices? The positioning of the ‘S’ on the port side doesn’t appear to have that same level of variation in the body, vertically.
Of course, NASA could have avoided having to work around that challenge by making the names of all the space shuttles palindromes.
This took me back to the time I didn’t spoke/read English very well, so I had to read the Brazilian version of Jalopnik. I thought that Raphael Orlove was a fellow Brazilian (same first name as me, save for the PH). Jalopnik Brasil was cut off from the main site around 2014, and what was left of it regrouped and became flatout.com.br, which was actually quite good, sort of a Brazilian version of the Autopian, but years before. Thanks for the trip down memory lane 🙂
I’ve been there 2x never noticed!! I bet it was an inside joke and it made no sense to correct, they would have to remove the blankets and replace them to redo the name.
In space, there is no “upside-down.”
“Next, we’ll draw a more different S…”
And now consummate (and thicker on the port side) Vs.
There’s a motorway sign near me (UK) where the number 8 is upside down.
Tried to find it on Google Maps, but no joy. I think there’s a truck blocking the view Obviously I’m not going to try and photograph it while driving.
It’s like the weavers who would make ornate oriental rugs by hand, only to tie one knot incorrectly, because “perfection is for the gods”. That saying is my standard response to someone saying “It’s not perfect, but…”
Several geeky/picky things I’ve never noticed:  typography glitches, body panel alignment, and bad-sounding MP3s.  I think I’m better off that they don’t bother me.
It all evened out on the launch pad when all the letters were rotated exactly 90 degrees.

articles.title_orig: Blaze that killed 4 soldiers on Canadian military base sparked on grenade launcher range, officials say
articles.title_zh: Blaze that killed 4 soldiers on Canadian military base sparked on grenade launcher range, officials say
articles.content_orig:
A blaze that killed four soldiers and injured several dozen more on a military base in the Canadian province of Alberta last week broke out on a grenade launcher range during training exercises, officials said Thursday.
The fire sparked Oct. 17 on the automatic grenade launcher range of Canadian Forces Base Wainwright "during routine military training activities," Brig. Gen. Vanessa Hanrahan, the Canadian Forces Provost Marshal, said in a statement Thursday.
The fire initially remained within the range's "Permanent Danger Area 2," which limited the ability of firefighters to battle it directly, Hanrahan said, and crews were forced to monitor it throughout the day instead.
However, it then spread due to "a subsequent change in wind direction and velocity" that "significantly increased the fire's intensity and rate of speed which led to these tragic events," Hanrahan added.
There was no indication that natural gas infrastructure was involved in the fire, she disclosed.
The fire killed four soldiers and injured 39 others. The Canadian Armed Forces said Thursday that 27 soldiers remained hospitalized, while 12 had been treated and released.
Earlier this week, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said that the fire was "driven by ferocious winds" and "jumped nearly a kilometer in less than a minute to where soldiers were gathered."
Carney said that 50 investigators had been brought in to probe the fire. The Canadian Forces National Investigation Service was leading the investigation, with support from the Royal Canadian Mounted Police.
"We will get the answers to what caused this terrible tragedy, as expeditiously and transparently as necessary," Carney told reporters Monday.
The fire overtook soldiers from the 3rd Battalion, Princess Patricia's Canadian Light Infantry, and Army reservists conducting live-fire training.
Maj. Gen. Wade Rutland said Sunday that military officials knew about the fire for hours but believed it was contained and allowed training to continue before winds suddenly shifted.
About 84 soldiers from Charlie Company were training at two locations, one for throwing grenades and another for practicing attacks on simulated enemy positions. The fire swept into the second area.
Carney said the soldiers were preparing for a mission next spring to reinforce Canadian troops serving with NATO in Latvia.
Rutland said investigators would examine whether winds drove the flames toward the soldiers or whether the fire spread unseen through vegetation. They will also examine whether military safety procedures need to change, he said.
The military identified those killed as Sgt. Morgan Wong of Edmonton; Pvt. Shaun Farrell of Prince Albert, Saskatchewan; Pvt. Aidan Goulding of North Vancouver, British Columbia; and Pvt. Hayden Lykkemark of Langley, British Columbia.

articles.title_orig: You Should Enable This Chrome Feature That Flags Suspicious Websites
articles.title_zh: You Should Enable This Chrome Feature That Flags Suspicious Websites
articles.content_orig:
Emily Long is a freelance writer based in Salt Lake City. After graduating from Duke University, she spent several years reporting on the federal workforce for Government Executive, a publication of Atlantic Media Company, in Washington, D.C. She has nearly a decade of experience as a freelancer covering tech (including issues related to security, privacy, and streaming) as well as personal finance and travel.
In addition to Lifehacker, her work has been featured on Wirecutter, Tom’s Guide, and ZDNET . Emily has also worked as a travel guide around the U.S. and as a content editor. She has a masters in social work and is a licensed therapist in Utah.
If you use Google Chrome, you can turn on a new safety feature that will warn you if you navigate to a suspicious website that looks like others already known for malicious behavior. The alerts are part of Enhanced Protection mode in Chrome's Safe Browsing, which checks your activity against potentially harmful sites and warns you if you're at risk of encountering malware, phishing, intrusive ads, or social engineering attacks.
Most internet users are familiar with the full-page alerts that appear if you navigate to a site that's known to be malicious. These red "dangerous site" warnings indicate a high risk of harm to the user and can't really be ignored since they take up the entire screen and urge you to go back to safety.
The new "suspicious site" alerts indicate possible risk of harm based on patterns consistent with other known malicious sites. This means that Google isn't as confident that the website is actually dangerous, but it looks a lot like others that are spreading malware or running phishing scams. These suspicious site warnings are smaller pop-ups with the text "This site doesn't seem right" and two button options: Mark as safe or Back to safety . The different colors, text, and formatting make it easy for users to distinguish between what Google deems dangerous versus suspicious.
Safe Browsing in Chrome has three options: standard protection, enhanced protection, and no protection at all (which isn't recommended). Standard protection checks your browsing activity, extensions, and downloads against Google's list of unsafe sites, which is updated periodically. By contrast, enhanced protection works in real time and uses AI analysis. Note that enhanced protection does require you to share more information about your activity to Google, and the data are linked to your Google Account.
While privacy-conscious users may be hesitant to send more info to Google, enhanced protection is likely worthwhile for those who aren't as savvy to advanced scam tactics (and therefore more likely to enter credentials or financial information on or download a file from a malicious website). To enable Enhanced Protection and receive suspicious website warnings, go to Settings > Privacy and security in Chrome and toggle Enhanced protection on under the Safe Browsing section.
Emily Long is a freelance writer based in Salt Lake City.

Blu-ray is fading after 20 years in the market, with Sony Japan finally discontinuing its last dedicated Blu-ray player. According to FlatpanelsHD , Sony Japan has finally marked the UBP-X700/K player as “Discontinued,” meaning customers in the country can no longer purchase a new standalone Blu-ray player from the company. This should not come as a surprise, as Sony stopped shipping the players in February of this year, suggesting that Sony only relied on existing inventory for its remaining Blu-ray player sales.
The PlayStation 5 is the only remaining Sony device that can play Blu-ray discs, but the company has also announced that it will end physical game disc production by January 2028. Because of this, some people fear that the upcoming PlayStation 6 will no longer have an optical drive. This move follows in the footsteps of LG , which ended Blu-ray player production in 2024. Japanese electronics companies Elecom and Buffalo have also ended production of Blu-ray drives for PCs this year, although Buffalo Americas says that it is “fully committed to supplying optical drives to the American market, and our DVD/Blu-ray drive products are anticipated to remain available for the near future.”
This move away from physical media and focus on streaming is worrying, especially to those who are concerned that we are moving towards a world where people no longer own anything. Because of this, sales of “retro media,” including CDs and vinyl, went up by 59% and 18% respectively . While you could still purchase a Blu-ray player from other manufacturers like Panasonic, Sony is one of the bigger companies that built and supported the standard, and its move to end the production and sale of Blu-ray players will leave this niche market even smaller. The audiophile market is facing the same dilemma, as some Hi-Fi player manufacturers ended production of selected products because optical drive makers have stopped making the components needed to read SACDs .
Ultra HD Blu-ray is facing the same upheaval that VHS and DVDs went through with the introduction of new formats. But while the older technologies were replaced by higher-quality formats, Blu-ray is being replaced not by more pixels, but by the convenience of streaming. However, it also comes with the caveat that people would no longer own physical media; a trend that worries data archivists.

Nintendo has added three more Game Boy games to the ever expanding Nintendo Switch Online library. The follow titles are now available on Switch and Switch 2: Pinball: Revenge of the ‘Gator (1989), Avenging Spirit (1992), and Mole Mania (1996). Last week, we received 3 Game Boy Advance titles exclusive to members of the NSO Expansion Pack, but original Game Boy games are available to anyone with a standard subscription. As always, these classic titles can be accessed from the “Game Boy – Nintendo Classics ” app that can be downloaded via the Nintendo eShop.

articles.title_orig: Exclusive | Chris LaCivita and James Blair donate full Bosnian consulting fee to Trump presidential library
articles.title_zh: Exclusive | Chris LaCivita and James Blair donate full Bosnian consulting fee to Trump presidential library
articles.content_orig:
WASHINGTON — President Trump’s election advisers Chris LaCivita and James Blair have donated their six-figure consulting fees from a controversial side-hustle in Bosnia and Herzegovina to Trump’s presidential library, The Post has learned.
Trump was “gloating” and “very braggadocious” in private conversations this week upon learning the development, a source said — indicating that his initial hard feelings toward LaCivita and Blair over their Eastern European gig had eased.
Another source confirmed Trump was pleased to hear of the donation.
The transfer was confirmed by four sources, two of whom said that Trump heard indirectly and not from the men about their decision.
LaCivita, who co-led Trump’s 2024 presidential campaign, and Blair, who served as a deputy chief of staff at the White House until May, likely will still have to pay income taxes on the revenue, which sources said was more than $100,000 apiece.
Trump had raged earlier this month after the New York Times reported that the duo, who hold top roles at the MAGA Inc super pac, had taken a trip to back a political party in the ethnically Serbian Republika Srpska, where they advised the victorious ruling party, led by Milorad Dodik, in the region’s election.
Dodik is friendly toward both Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
The side job gave the impression that LaCivita and Blair were enriching themselves off their connection to Trump and taking their eyes off beleaguered Republican congressional campaigns — though some of their colleagues described them as remaining engaged remotely in the US election work.
“Chris LaCivita and James Blair are outside consultants. They do not work for me, other than as outside consultants. They most likely have numerous clients, but for that, you would have to ask them,” Trump fumed on Truth Social in his initial response on Oct. 7.
“They are allowed to do work for others, just like all consultants in Washington, D.C. I do not have any idea who else they work for but will, on reflection, ask them and, if there’s a conflict, I will terminate them, immediately!”
Blair, who masterminded a Republican redistricting drive this year to redraw House districts to favor the GOP, accompanied Trump to a campaign rally in South Carolina on Wednesday, indicating a thaw.
A White House official told The Post on Thursday that Trump did not seem to be upset with Blair or likely to blame him if Republicans are wiped out on Nov. 3, describing their conversations as businesslike and tactical.

articles.title_orig: Wealthy Chinese move offshore money to U.S. banks as Beijing’s tax net widens
articles.title_zh: Wealthy Chinese move offshore money to U.S. banks as Beijing’s tax net widens
articles.content_orig:
SINGAPORE —  Wealthy Chinese rattled by Beijing's widening hunt for overseas wealth are turning to a once-familiar refuge for their money: the U.S.
Private bankers and lawyers who work with Chinese clients say inquiries about opening U.S. bank accounts have grown in the months after Beijing imposed retroactive taxes on offshore wealth in July, moving assets previously stored in Singapore or Hong Kong there to stay further away from Beijing's reach.
"It has become relatively prevalent," said Keith Tan, CEO of Singapore-based Golden Acacia Capital, who is helping Chinese clients manage their offshore portfolios. His clients began planning exits to the U.S. in July, and some have the accounts set up in less than two months. "The hurdle is not that high for Chinese clients to open American accounts and transfer assets there."
Wealthy clients tend to choose large private banks while smaller accounts go to regional banks or online brokers, Tan said.
The rush has gained urgency with China's new tax regime on offshore trusts. Authorities said in July that income and gains from overseas trusts owned by Chinese tax residents would be taxed at 20%, setting off a scramble for cash and alternative structures .
Lawyers in Singapore and Hong Kong have been working to tally how much tax their clients owe, facilitating trusts' unwinding, sales of shares in listed companies or applying for loans to meet the outsized tax bill.
Meanwhile, the U.S. sits outside the Common Reporting Standard, or CRS, the OECD framework under which more than 100 jurisdictions automatically share financial account data. While banks in Singapore and Hong Kong are supposed to report China-linked accounts to Beijing, American banks have no such obligation.
Non-resident clients who open foreign bank accounts in the U.S. can also find investment vehicles with reduced or no tax-filing obligations to the Internal Revenue Service, said James Wang, CEO of Blue Brick Consulting Group, a private-client tax advisor. But China's latest regulations require people classified as Chinese tax residents to self-declare worldwide income to Beijing, Wang said.
Banks in New York are seizing the opportunity to offer a solution that could shield Chinese customers from their country's tax man. U.S. banks are straining to keep up with the rise in demand, according to a New York-based wealth-planning advisor who works with Chinese family offices.
"With inquiries surging, some banks have shortened the timeframe for clients to meet required minimum capital commitments" before the accounts are subject to closure, said the advisor, who requested anonymity to speak about bank processes.
Chinese families with offspring holding U.S. green cards have also used foreign grantor trusts – structures treated as owned by their non-American founder – to shield them from some tax exposure in the U.S., Tan said. Low-tax states such as Nevada and Florida have become popular choices, he added.
"They are gambling on not being disclosed, because the U.S. does not share information as part of the CRS system; they can dodge tax authorities," said Clifford Ng, a partner at Zhong Lun law firm in Hong Kong. Ng also expects that some with Hong Kong or Singapore residency whose trusts have not yet been flagged to Beijing may unwind those structures and transfer the money out.
Lawyers caution that though the route works for now to avoid disclosure, it may be temporary. Money held offshore has probably already been reported to Beijing through the CRS and would "have shown up in China at some point," Ng said, so a transfer from a Singapore or Hong Kong bank to a U.S. one would be visible on its way out.
"They may still be in breach of the rules because they have an undisclosed offshore account that's making money and they're not declaring it onshore," Ng said. "Hiding is not tax planning."
Washington's Foreign Account Tax Compliance Act requires foreign banks to report American clients, but so far there's no matching automatic flow from U.S. banks to Beijing.
Cris Cao, Beijing-based partner at W&H Law Firm, agreed on the risk of Beijing's ability to tax money moved to the U.S. "Even if they move all the money out of the CRS-reported accounts and into U.S. bank accounts, that doesn't naturally reduce or wipe out the tax authorities' right to tax, or their obligation to pay," he said.
"There was a record of it being transferred out," Cao said, and "that alone is enough for the tax authorities to levy tax."
What's more, the window of opportunity may have closed. Moving money that is already offshore around is relatively easy, but getting capital out of mainland China has become increasingly difficult.
"Nearly no sizeable money onshore will be able to leave the country from now on," said Jingkuan Lin, a private banker at Bank of Singapore, who sees the offshore banking industry being further limited to serving the existing pool of capital outside China.

articles.title_orig: Jared Kushner Blasts ‘Outrageous’ Vanity Fair Over Report On Alleged Undisclosed Foreign Bank Accounts
articles.title_zh: Jared Kushner Blasts ‘Outrageous’ Vanity Fair Over Report On Alleged Undisclosed Foreign Bank Accounts
articles.content_orig:
In late spring 2020, a source I knew to be reliable called me with a story. The Dutch government had hacked into Jared Kushner ’s phone and monitored him as he accessed a Dubai-based bank account. What was odd, the source said, was that the money in the account—hundreds of millions of dollars—had come from a bank in Azerbaijan. Most importantly, Kushner appeared to have transferred significant amounts of money from the Dubai account to other individuals, including a warlord, a mercenary and a one-time hit man. The story sounded preposterous, I told my source. And yet.
Six months later, I found myself speaking with someone else about the UAE government and their use of mercenaries in conflicts around the Middle East and Africa when I asked, on a whim, whether they knew anything about Kushner and bank transfers from a UAE account. My acquaintance grew quiet. Then they replied, “Yes.”
Over the next four years, I came to learn that, sometime in late 2017, the Netherlands Defense Intelligence and Security Service (MIVD) made a startling discovery. A General Staff of the Armed Forces of the Russian Federation (GRU) operative, a dark web hacker specializing in stolen bank data, was traveling to the UK for an espionage mission. They reached out to the British government for permission to apprehend him when he arrived. The British agreed.
When the Russian national arrived in England, the Dutch informed him that he had two options: he could work for them against the GRU, or the British would arrest him. Once in UK government custody, the operative would be charged with espionage. If convicted, he would spend years in a British prison. The Russian chose to change his employer.
Later that year, the Russian operative gave the Dutch spies access to one of the GRU’s most sensitive assets. Located in Rostov, Russia, the GRU’s hacking and cyber team operated a remote server on which they stored some of their bounty. During their search through these secret files, the Dutch found something astonishing: screenshots of Jared Kushner’s iPhone.
In The Hague, the MIVD hacking team tried to reverse engineer the Russian penetration of Kushner’s iPhone. Kushner owned what was then the latest model, the iPhone X. Released in November 2017, it featured Face ID, a state-of-the-art security feature that Apple had promoted at its launch. The Dutch team had been trying to pick the phone’s door lock, so to speak, when it occurred to them that the Russians may have found an unlocked window to gain entry instead. Their hypothesis was correct. By early 2018, the MIVD had found a vulnerability in the iPhone that gave them access. The security exploit wasn’t perfect, however. Some malware allows a hacker to turn a victim’s phone into a microphone and video camera, turn the phone on or off, and pull and add files. The Dutch solution did not provide that level of access. Instead, when Kushner used the phone, they could see his screen. Almost as soon as they got inside, the intelligence service began capturing every image of Kushner’s screen as he used it, filing their own cache of surveillance on their internal computer servers.
As they monitored Kushner’s phone, they discovered he used it to log in to a UAE bank account. By the time the Dutch spies had visibility into the phone, the account had received hundreds of millions of dollars from a bank in Azerbaijan. Their initial assessment was that the bank account was affiliated with the government there.
For the MIVD hackers, the bank account became an intelligence mystery to unravel. Nearly everything they worked on had a tinge of Russian conspiracy. A little over a year into Trump’s first presidency, the MIVD, like FBI agents and federal prosecutors in Washington working on the Robert Mueller investigation, had only part of the story.
Kushner, UAE ruler Mohamed bin Zayed (MBZ) and Mohammed bin Salman (MBS) of Saudi Arabia, converged at an auspicious moment. MBS wanted to be crown prince. MBZ wanted to blow up Obama’s Iran nuclear deal, and Kushner wanted both to help him force the Palestinians into a deal that Israel would accept. Despite the perception of his wealth, Kushner was not entirely financially independent of his parents, and the family business, Kushner Companies, faced a billion-dollar loan coming due on their trophy property, the Manhattan office building at 666 Fifth Avenue.
Early in the first Trump administration, MBZ and MBS offered to pay for a slush fund dedicated to helping the new administration with foreign policy goals. The idea was to help pay for Trump’s promised wall between Mexico and the US, for example, in an effort to secure a second term in the White House. The two Arab royals initially discussed with Kushner putting more than $10 billion into the effort. Within months, though, as MBZ pushed the Trump administration to help back MBS’s effort to become his country’s crown prince—and future king—the broader foreign policy slush fund idea fizzled. Instead, MBZ and MBS initially, and then MBZ alone, put at least $2 billion into at least two bank accounts for Kushner. It is unclear how the royals organized their $2 billion in combined payments, but they effectively split the cost. For the purposes of explanation, it is best to understand where and how each bank account was controlled.
Bank account Alpha was held at First Abu Dhabi Bank, the largest in the UAE, and was overseen by MBZ’s brother, Tahnoon bin Zayed, who served as the bank’s chairman. Beginning in 2017, the Saudis and Emiratis transferred roughly $750 million into the Alpha account. Alpha would be used as a foreign policy fund. This money would be overseen and partially managed by Kushner and MBZ, who, in their effort to strike a grand bargain to end the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, believed the region’s map needed to be redrawn.
“Jared was looking for shortcuts in his diplomacy,” a source who knew of the UAE’s deal with Kushner said. This person held discussions with both senior UAE and Israeli officials about the secret financial arrangement between Kushner, the UAE, and, at least initially, Saudi Arabia. “Jared promised MBZ that he’d push their agenda with Trump if they participated in a fund. He wanted normalization with Israel so that business could take off.” A slush fund—a shared pool of money for off-the-books diplomatic objectives—was a common form of Gulf Arab government corruption, this person explained. “The Emiratis and the Saudis do this once a year. A billion or two is nothing for them, and if it gets them what they want, it’s money well spent.”
The Alpha account looked like the funding source of a UAE government program, by which MBZ paid his bureaucrats their salaries or funded government-run schools. But how and through whom the money flowed into the Alpha account revealed that it was intended to remain secret, more akin to a covert and illicit scheme, given that it was managed in part by a senior advisor to the president of the United States.
The Dutch spies who monitored the Alpha account noted that all of it was sent by a bank in Azerbaijan in American dollars. Azerbaijan plays a unique role in money laundering. Its central bank maintains high levels of US dollars in its reserves but does not adhere to the highest standards of bank transparency. As a result, Azerbaijani banks have well-established but unadvertised practices of serving as way stations for large transfers, in which a foreign currency is exchanged for an equal amount in dollars. For a roughly 6 to 7 percent fee on the transaction, some Azerbaijani banks will accept a transfer from a client who wishes to move Saudi riyals or Emirati dirhams totaling hundreds of millions of dollars. The Saudi or Emirati client sends the money to the Azerbaijani bank, which then uses a different internal bank account to transfer the equivalent US dollars to the client’s requested destination. For auditors, this shadow trade can’t be discerned.

articles.title_orig: Rare unrest flares in Tunisian capital as police clash with protesters
articles.title_zh: Rare unrest flares in Tunisian capital as police clash with protesters
articles.content_orig:
Tunisian police have clashed with protesters in rare unrest in the capital city of Tunis, as well as ⁠⁠in the southern town of Jebiniana, over recent deaths linked to the police.
Police forces fired tear gas on Thursday to disperse protesters in ⁠⁠Ettadhamen, a suburb ⁠⁠of the capital, following the death of a man detained on suspicion of drug dealing.
The man’s family said he died as a result of abuse by police officers after his arrest, ‌‌calling for the circumstances of his death to be clarified and those responsible to be held accountable.
Local media, however, reported that he died after swallowing drugs.
Protesters blocked roads, burned tyres and threw stones at police. Security forces responded by firing tear gas while seeking ⁠⁠to secure a National Guard station in ⁠⁠the area, the Reuters news agency reported.
In Jebiniana, in Sfax governorate, police clashed with protesters following the death of a man whose relatives said he had died while being chased by security forces.
Tunisian media reported that protesters set a vehicle ablaze and burned tyres, while police used tear gas against the protesters.
Students in the coastal city of Sfax protested another civilian death, this time blaming ambulance services for the death of a female student who suffered a cardiac problem.
Her colleagues said ambulance personnel took too long to arrive, citing a lack of medical facilities, and ‌‌called for a strike at Sfax University’s faculties on Friday.
The flare-ups on Thursday coincide with a deepening economic, social and political crisis in Tunisia, heightening ⁠⁠fears of a wider wave of violent protests as anger grows over deteriorating living conditions and poor public services.
Thousands of Tunisians joined the largest protest against President Kais Saied in years in the ‌‌capital ‌‌on Saturday, accusing him of undermining democracy and mishandling the economy in a growing challenge to his rule.
A Tunisian military court on Wednesday sentenced opposition ⁠⁠politician Olfa ⁠⁠Hamdi to four years in prison on charges of plotting against state security and inciting the ⁠⁠military to disobey orders, the latest move against opponents of ⁠⁠Saied.

articles.title_orig: El Salvador deploys special forces to Haiti to help find 4 missing soldiers who came under attack
articles.title_zh: El Salvador deploys special forces to Haiti to help find 4 missing soldiers who came under attack
articles.content_orig:
El Salvador has deployed troops to Haiti to try to rescue four Salvadoran service members believed to have been captured by Haitian gangs, according to a spokesperson for the UN-authorized multinational security mission in Haiti known as the Gang Suppression Force (GSF).
The missing service members, described as non-combatant aviation technicians that were supporting the GSF mission, were ambushed by gangs on October 18, Salvadoran officials have said.
The GSF has been carrying out a dayslong operation to try to find them. The effort has resulted in armed clashes that have left at least seven gang members dead and four GSF personnel wounded, the GSF has said.
A spokesperson for the security mission confirmed to CNN on Thursday Salvadoran troops had arrived in Haiti to support the effort.
The Miami Herald first reported that a 100-strong team was deployed. El Salvador has not commented on the specific details of the mission.
It comes a day after Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele announced that his country had launched an unspecified “military operation” to rescue the missing men.
Bukele, who has carried out a brutal crackdown on gangs in his own country, warned Haitian gang members that they would face a more severe response if they didn’t release the service members alive.
“And do not take our word for empty threats. We have already finished with the gangs in El Salvador, and we can finish with you too,” he said on X.
Gang leader Lanmo Sanjou issued a response to Bukele on Thursday, filming himself with large quantities of ammunition and warning that his group would “fight to stay alive.”
The GSF was established by the UN Security Council in 2025 to help Haiti fight the gangs plaguing the country . According to the resolution adopted at that time, the force consists of 5,500 military or police personnel and 50 civilians from various nations. El Salvador is one of the countries that agreed to provide personnel. Bukele says their primary job is to carry out medical evacuations.
CNN’s Mauricio Torres contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: Microsoft Announces Per-Hour Cost for Xbox Cloud Gaming Service
articles.title_zh: Microsoft Announces Per-Hour Cost for Xbox Cloud Gaming Service
articles.content_orig:
Xbox has revealed the pricing for the cloud gaming limits on Game Pass, announced last month .
Referred to as cloud playtime packs, launch pricing is 10 hours for $3.99, 25 hours for $7.99, and 50 hours for $11.99.
These packs offer ad-free cloud gaming with shorter wait times and high-quality streaming. Playtime remains available until it's used.
Xbox Insiders who don't have a Game Pass subscription can currently preview the pricing options before they roll out in November. They can also try ad-supported game streaming , which Xbox began testing earlier this year.
Xbox noted that "availability, purchasing options, eligible games, and cloud gaming options may vary by market, device, account eligibility, and preview ring."
As announced last month, Game Pass Essential will be limited to five hours, Premium to ten hours, and Ultimate to fifteen hours.
The decision was made due to "the cost of providing cloud gaming grows as more people use it and play for longer."
"Moving to monthly limits allows us to keep offering the service while continuing to invest in its reliability and performance. We understand that for some players the practical result is a higher cost."
Yesterday, reports suggested that Xbox is planning an overhaul of Game Pass.
This could include the ability for players to select "add-ons for console-only games, cloud gaming, and multiplayer, with the system operating on a tiered structure."

articles.title_zh: China-made cancer drug to go on sale in US after Americans travel to buy it
articles.content_orig:
AstraZeneca moves to make the lung cancer treatment available in the US after lengthy delays raised concerns over patient access
Global pharmaceutical firm AstraZeneca said on Thursday it would start selling a cancer drug after coming under criticism for failing to bring it to the US market faster, prompting some Americans to fly to Shanghai to procure the potentially life-saving medicine first developed by China.
In recent months, desperate Americans have travelled to China to obtain the Chinese-made cancer drug that was approved by the US Food and Drug Administration but remained unavailable in the country for more than a year, according to a cancer-treatment awareness advocate who made the journey while his mother was battling the disease.
Developed by China’s Dizal Pharmaceutical, sunvozertinib is a targeted lung cancer drug designed to treat adults with an advanced form of the illness, offering another treatment option for patients.
“The drug was approved in China in 2023. The FDA approved it in July 2025,” Max Doppelt, chief executive of Patient Data Vault, a consultancy that connects cancer patients to clinical trials, wrote on social media on Wednesday.

articles.title_orig: GTA 6 Standard Edition vs. Ultimate Edition: Which Version Is the Better Deal?
articles.title_zh: GTA 6 Standard Edition vs. Ultimate Edition: Which Version Is the Better Deal?
articles.content_orig:
Getting your Trinity Audio player ready...
Grand Theft Auto VI is almost here, so it’s time to make your final preparations. Watch the extended gameplay footage ? Check. Revisit the nostalgia of Vice City ? Check. Pick which console you’ll use to play? Check. All that’s left now is to preorder , right? Actually, there’s one more choice to make because GTA 6 comes in two versions: the Standard Edition and Ultimate Edition. But which should you purchase? Let us help you make the decision.
Both editions of GTA 6 launch on Nov. 19 for the same platforms (PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S). The most obvious difference is price. The Standard Edition costs $80, which is already higher than the typical price even for a modern blockbuster video game. Meanwhile, the Ultimate Edition costs $100, not uncommon for a deluxe version of the game, but still potentially a hard pill to swallow. If you’ve already purchased the Standard Edition, you can also pay to upgrade to the Ultimate Edition.
Both editions promise a version of the GTA 6 that should feel plenty complete. But what do you get with the Ultimate Edition to make it worth the premium upgrade? Put another way, what does the Standard Edition lack?
GTA 6 Ultimate Edition includes a variety of extra weapons, cosmetics, and cars. If you want to drive around in a ‘95 Grotti Cheetah while getting into shootouts with Hawk & Little Morgan Revolvers, this is the only way. This version also unlocks new storefronts for accessing exclusive content, such as salons and tattoo parlors to further customize your character, or shops to mod your guns. "Ultimate Edition bonuses are threaded across all aspects of Jason and Lucia's story, with new items uncovered behind each chapter," Rockstar says .
There are also preorder bonuses available on both versions. Buy GTA 6 before Nov. 20, and you’ll unlock additional retro weapons, outfits, and vehicles inspired by the 1980s version of Vice City. You also get one month of GTA+ , Rockstar’s membership for Grand Theft Auto Online, an $8 value.
It’s hard to look at these two versions and not feel that the one with more stuff is the better, fuller experience. “It's the culmination of that really obnoxious trend where studios develop a game then chop it up to sell back to you later as DLC,” said my colleague Gabe Zamora , expressing frustration over the split. “In this case, they're literally launching with two versions of the game: one has all the customizations and features available at launch, and the cheaper version cuts down on that to package the product at a ‘discount price.’ It gives Rockstar a way to charge 100 bucks for a game without looking like bad guys.”
So, even if it feels a bit scummy, if you’re already paying $80 for a game, there’s an argument to be made that you might as well go for the full $100 version just to sample everything on offer. However, when I actually look at the Ultimate perks, it’s all seemingly supplemental material, not core aspects of the game itself. New styles and guns are nice to have, but it’s not like the Standard Edition won’t have plenty of those already.
Our recommendation? If you’re a true diehard and plan to immerse yourself in GTA 6 for weeks and months to come, you’ll easily get your money’s worth out of the Ultimate Edition. But if you’re less sure, if you’re just playing the game because you’re curious about the hype, stick with Standard at launch, and upgrade later if you’re still hungry for more.
My PCMag career began in 2013 as an intern. Now, I'm a senior writer, using the skills I acquired at Northwestern University to write about dating apps, meal kits, programming software, website builders, video streaming services, and video games. I was previously a senior editor at Geek.com and have written for The A.V. Club, Kotaku, and Paste Magazine. I'm the author of the gaming history book Video Game of the Year: A Year-by-Year Guide to the Best, Boldest, and Most Bizarre Games from Every Year Since 1977 , and the reason everything you know about Street Sharks is a lie.

articles.title_orig: Solidigm to Discontinue Review of Potential IPO, Reaffirming Commitment to Long-Term Growth and Shareholder Value
articles.title_zh: Solidigm to Discontinue Review of Potential IPO, Reaffirming Commitment to Long-Term Growth and Shareholder Value
articles.content_orig:
Solidigm will halt its review of potential pre-IPO and IPO options.
This decision does not reflect any change in Solidigm’s growth prospects or investment needs. Rather, in light of recent capital market conditions and share price trends, Solidigm determined that it was necessary to reassess whether an IPO would be the most beneficial option for SK hynix and its existing shareholders at this time.
Growing memory demand in the AI era presents new growth opportunities for Solidigm. However, its existing production facilities have limited capacity to meet rising demand, making it necessary for U.S.-based Solidigm to secure additional production facilities in the U.S.
To secure the funding needed for Solidigm’s growth and ensure efficient capital allocation, SK hynix has been evaluating various options, including direct investment in Solidigm and raising external capital through an IPO.
Raising external capital through an IPO could increase SK hynix’s consolidated cash flow, creating greater capacity to fund facility investments while also supporting shareholder returns through dividends, share repurchases, and share cancellations.
Furthermore, if Solidigm were to achieve an appropriate valuation through an IPO, the market could recognize its growth potential more fully—a potential that is not adequately reflected in SK hynix’s current corporate value.
Ultimately, the IPO review was an effort to identify options that would secure funding for Solidigm’s growth while enhancing the economic value of SK hynix’s existing shareholders’ holdings.
While SK hynix and Solidigm continue to deliver solid business performance, financial market volatility has increased, contributing to a broader correction in semiconductor stocks.
After comprehensively assessing these business conditions, Solidigm has decided to discontinue its review of potential pre-IPO and IPO options.
Expanding Solidigm’s production capacity and strengthening its competitiveness remain important priorities.
SK hynix will also continue to assess investment timing, scale, and financing methods while exploring various options to support Solidigm’s growth and enhance value for existing shareholders.

articles.title_orig: Elon Musk’s $10.5B SpaceX gift to kids has a catch: Families can’t say no — and may need to wait 5 years to cash out
articles.title_zh: Elon Musk’s $10.5B SpaceX gift to kids has a catch: Families can’t say no — and may need to wait 5 years to cash out
articles.content_orig:
SpaceX said on Thursday that its stake in Elon Musk's The Boring Co. netted the company an investment gain of $561 million during the third quarter.
The gain accounted for more than half of SpaceX's "other income" in the period and boosted its net income, which landed at just over $4 billion, the company said in its quarterly financial filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission.
Created inside SpaceX in 2017 and spun out a year later, Boring Co. says its mission is to "revolutionize transportation" by creating underground tunnels with stations where passengers can board and exit. Last month, Boring Co. raised $3 billion at a $23 billion valuation, with backing from the United Arab Emirates and a roster of other longtime Musk supporters.
Boring Co. has announced about a dozen city projects, but its only tunnels currently open for public use  are in Las Vegas, where passengers can travel in Tesla vehicles between the downtown convention center and various casino resorts using its Las Vegas Convention Center Loop.
In July of last year, Boring Co. struck a deal to build about 20 miles of tunnels in Nashville, Tennessee. The Music City Loop, as it's known, is being designed to carry paying passengers between downtown and the airport in Tesla vehicles. The fast-tracked project sparked a partisan feud when it was greenlit and has drawn new safety concerns over sinkhole risks this week.
In the UAE, Boring Co. plans to build over 150 kilometers (93 miles) of tunnels, including a project announced in February of last year, the Dubai Loop.
SpaceX also said in Thursday's filing that it purchased $151 million worth of Tesla's Megapack energy storage systems during the quarter. Musk said on SpaceX's earnings call on Tuesday that he thinks it would be a "good idea" for the two companies to merge, and said they've both created special committees to discuss a potential transaction.

articles.title_orig: The next-gen Xbox won’t cost you $1,800. It can’t. Can it?
articles.title_zh: The next-gen Xbox won’t cost you $1,800. It can’t. Can it?
articles.content_orig:
When you buy through links on our articles, Future and its syndication partners may earn a commission.
Credit: Microsoft / Future
Former Blizzard president Mike Ybarra doesn't like what he's hearing about the next Xbox console costing somewhere in the range of $1,200 to $1,800, as was recently reported.
In case you hadn't heard, yes, I'm afraid I bring you even more bad news about the games console market . A recent report from Fortune claims Microsoft is projecting internally that its next home console will "cost consumers between $1,200 and $1,800," assuming Xbox doesn't subsidize some of that cost and take a potential financial loss on hardware sales. Even amid an unprecedented increase in component costs driven by global memory shortages , $1,800 is stretching the limits of the most cynical predictions for the price of next-gen hardware. Let's remember quickly that less than six years ago, the PS5 and Xbox Series X released for $500.
Voicing his astonishment at the possibility on Twitter, Ybarra urges Xbox against considering a next-gen line of consoles at such an exorbitant cost to consumers.
"I find this very hard to believe," he says. "A 'console' is a mass-audience device and you need great games and a low entry price (IMO $399 to $499). A console at the prices rumored below will never sell meaningful units to be of any value vs. alternatives. Zero.
"I wouldn't release it at all," says Ybarra.
I find this very hard to believe. A "console" is a mass-audience device and you need great games and a low entry price (IMO $399 to $499). A console at the prices rumored below will never sell meaningful units to be of any value vs. alternatives. Zero. I wouldn't release it at all. Stick with PS5 Pro/Series X until prices normalize. The capabilities of those boxes are both fine for 99% of the audience. No one is screaming "I need a more powerful console" right now and I believe tons of optimization can and is happening on those platforms (see Xbox's AMD announcement on FSR 4.1 today - which is fantastic).
— @Qwik (October 20, 2026)
Not to belabor the point, but consumers particularly in the US right now are already fielding increased prices on everything from fuel to housing to insurance to ground beef, and entertainment as an expense is increasingly being squeezed from budgets. Anecdotally, I can tell you that if Xbox released a $1,200 console today, I would simply dust off my Xbox Series X and tell new Xbox to get bent. And that's exactly what Ybarra suggests console manufacturers do for now:
"Stick with PS5 Pro/Series X until prices normalize. The capabilities of those boxes are both fine for 99% of the audience," he says. "No one is screaming 'I need a more powerful console' right now and I believe tons of optimization can and is happening on those platforms." As an example of these optimizations, Ybarra points to Xbox's recent announcement that its machine-learning upscaler FSR 4.1 is coming to Xbox Series X and S.
I'm interested to see how Xbox navigates this situation. Amid new CEO Asha Sharma's big and layoff-heavy reset , what the company does with its next big machine will answer a ton of questions about how it plans to position itself against competitors Sony and Nintendo in the next generation of hardware. Of course, Sony and Nintendo are in similar predicaments, although Nintendo to a lesser degree as it just released the Switch 2 last year.
If the idea of an $1,800 Xbox that doesn't even run physical games horrifies you, I'd pick up an Evercade Nexus and ignore the next generation

articles.title_orig: Moderna, Merck shares fall on eagerly anticipated cancer vaccine results
articles.title_zh: Moderna, Merck shares fall on eagerly anticipated cancer vaccine results
articles.content_orig:
A regimen involving the vaccine cut the risk of relapse or death by 42% in a landmark melanoma study that met investor expectations but triggered a “sell-the-news” response, one analyst wrote.
A cancer vaccine developed by Moderna and Merck & Co. has lived up to its billing, meeting lofty expectations from industry watchers and physicians in slowing the return of advanced melanoma, according to data published ahead of a major medical meeting.
Moderna and Merck reported in August that a combination of the vaccine, “intismeran autogene,” and Merck’s immunotherapy Keytruda, bested Keytruda alone in a late-stage trial. That study evaluated both regimens in the “adjuvant” setting after surgical removal of a tumor.
The companies didn’t disclose details from the trial at the time, only noting that the combination had met its main goal at an early, pre-planned data check. Nonetheless, the results were hailed by analysts as a “landmark moment” and evidence that intismeran is destined for billions of dollars in sales. Moderna’s stock price swelled more than four-fold afterwards.
The announcement made a coming Saturday presentation from the trial at the European Society for Medical Oncology meeting this year one of the biotechnology sector’s most eagerly anticipated. Ahead of it, Wall Street investors expected the intismeran regimen to be associated with anywhere from 40% to 50% relative reduction in the risk of disease recurrence or death.
Moderna had already stated a 35% lowering would constitute a clinically significant outcome, which itself was a high bar considering Keytruda alone hit the 43% mark when compared to a placebo.
Screenshots of the findings were leaked on social media Thursday, prompting ESMO to immediately release the closely guarded study details before the meeting. According to those findings, intismeran met its mark, as the combination cut the relative risk of disease recurrence or death by 42% compared to Keytruda alone after a median of 24.6 months.
The results fall a touch short of the 44% figure initially observed in a smaller and similarly closely watched Phase 2 trial. Long-term results from that study were even more profound, showing that the risk of relapse was nearly cut in half after five years of follow-up.
Shares of both companies immediately fell on the news, with Moderna’s stock price tumbling by nearly 25% and Merck’s by around 1%.
Some analysts immediately rallied to both companies’ defense. A “sell-the-news reaction is playing out,” wrote William Blair analyst Myles Minter. The findings "represent a highly compelling efficacy profile and substantially clear the [physician]-defined bar for a practice-changing dataset in adjuvant melanoma,” added TD Cowen analyst Tyler Van Buren.
RBC Capital Markets analyst Trung Huynh, however, noted that the results were on the “low end” of expectations and showed a "deterioration" from what was seen in earlier testing.
“While approval seems likely, commercial success is far less certain,” Huynh wrote.
Investigators interviewed by BioPharma Dive argued that the data represent a possible step forward in care for a persistent type of cancer.
Even with the availability of Keytruda — one of the most successful cancer drugs in history — one-third or more of people diagnosed with late-stage melanoma will die or see their disease return within five years of treatment. Drugmakers have struggled mightily to improve upon those numbers, with “PD-1” inhibitors like Keytruda as well as other medications.
“We have tried really hard. I have led clinical trials. None of them has improved over PD-1,” said Hussein Tawbi, a professor of medicine at the MD Anderson Cancer Center and an investigator in Moderna and Merck’s study. “We were resigned to the fact that this was the best we can do for patients. And now we see we can do better.”
Adding intismeran to Keytruda also reduced the relative risk of cancer spreading to “distant” organs or tissues by 38% versus Keytruda alone, researchers found.
The trial enrollees who got intismeran reported similar rates of side effects, although those recipients had a substantially higher frequency of fever and injection-site pain. About 7% of the people who got intismeran discontinued treatment because of an adverse event, compared with 5% of those in the comparator group.
The risk of these side effects is likely “something a lot of patients would be willing to take on” given their chance to live longer, said Janice Mehnert, director of melanoma and cutaneous medical oncology at NYU Langone Health. Mehnert was also involved in the study.
The results are the product of decades of research into vaccines that can train the body’s immune system to better recognize and hunt down cancer cells. Several earlier projects failed because they didn’t trigger a strong enough immune response, stimulated the wrong immune cells or couldn’t overcome tumors’ ability to thwart the body’s defenses. But more recently, developers like Moderna have turned to mRNA technology popularized by COVID-19 vaccines to come up with a newer approach.
This strategy is known as “individualized neoantigen therapy.” It involves sequencing a patient’s tumor to find cancer-specific protein flags, or “neoantigens,” and then delivering into cells mRNA that encodes for them. Their presence sparks a response from immune defenders called T cells to hunt down and destroy any cells with those proteins.
Intismeran teaches the body to spot up to 34 neoantigens. Another developer, BioNTech, has an individualized therapy in testing in colorectal and pancreatic cancer.
Moderna and Merck have now shown the approach can work in melanoma. But physicians and investors aren’t yet sure how broadly impactful it might be in other types of cancer or in earlier stage disease. BioNTech recently reported that its personalized vaccine failed a mid-stage trial in colorectal cancer.
Merck and Moderna are running additional studies in lung, bladder and kidney cancer. Interim results from a mid-stage trial in kidney tumors could come later this year or in the first half of 2027, RBC analyst Huynh recently wrote in a note to investors.

articles.title_orig: Macron blames ‘seditious’ far left for unrest as France bans some protests
articles.title_zh: Macron blames ‘seditious’ far left for unrest as France bans some protests
articles.content_orig:
French authorities have barred demonstrations in several of the country’s largest cities, as President Emmanuel Macron blamed far-left groups for stoking violence during weekend protests .
The Paris Police Prefecture announced that Thursday’s protests would be banned in key parts of the city until 8pm (18:00 GMT). That includes areas near the presidential Elysee Palace, both houses of parliament, the city’s main train stations, as well as parts of downtown where looting occurred over the weekend.
A police source told the AFP news agency the ban was necessary due to organisers’ “inability to prevent violence and vandalism”.
Elsewhere in France, authorities also prohibited protests planned for Thursday in Lyon, Lille and Grenoble.
The restrictions come after more than half a million people gathered across France on Saturday in a protest that brought together students demanding better conditions in schools and groups denouncing high living costs.
France’s ⁠justice minister Gerald Darmanin said on Thursday that at least 2,700 people had been taken into custody after riots broke out in several areas , and shops were looted. Darmanin added that 217 of those arrested had already been convicted and jailed. 1,000 others were being prosecuted.
President Macron blamed Saturday’s riots on what he called “seditious acts” by “ultra-left” groups, whom he accused of trying to “bring down the Republic”.
Speaking from the Elysee Palace on Thursday, Macron said France would ban all “illegitimate” protests in the coming days, while approved demonstrations led by organised groups like unions would be required to take alternative routes outside city centres to protect businesses .
He added that he would convene the country’s defence council on Friday to take further action.
Thursday’s planned protests were seen as a prelude to a large demonstration on Saturday, when activists from the “yellow vest” movement, whose demonstrations over fuel prices shook France in 2018 and 2019, are expected to join.
Some of those protests, including marches in Lyon, will also be banned, local authorities said after hours of “chaos” last weekend when more than 200 shops were looted.
Officials for the Bouche-du-Rhone region covering France’s second-largest city Marseille has also banned all protests there on Saturday citing “obvious reasons of security”.
The French government said the Louvre, Orsay and Picasso museums in Paris would remain closed on Saturday due to new planned demonstrations.
Jean-Luc Melenchon, a far-left candidate for next year’s presidential election criticised by the government for not strongly condemning the protest violence, blamed authorities’ “non-stop brutal repression” for the unrest.
“On Saturday, the army is guarding buildings instead of the police, and the Paris police prefect is asking shopkeepers to call on private security guards…,” Melenchon said in a post on X.
Meanwhile Marine Le Pen, the far-right leader currently topping opinion polls, accused Macron’s government of being too soft and lacking authority.
Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu, who met union representatives on Wednesday, said a “massive” security operation was planned for Saturday to prevent a repeat of the violence by small groups of rioters that had exposed shortcomings in security measures.
Meanwhile, Macron held a meeting with intelligence services, Lecornu and ministers on Thursday morning to obtain a detailed account of what went wrong over the weekend and review preparations for upcoming protests.
Union representatives said their meeting with Lecornu did not result in concrete proposals. They are now focusing on another big day of action scheduled for November 5, calling on private and public sector employees to join.
The education demonstrations first erupted last month in a high school in Creteil, southeast of Paris, over a lack of staff.
From there, class strikes, blockades and demonstrations spread to other Paris suburbs and then nationwide, including in smaller towns.
High school students have raised concerns about underfunded schools, dilapidated facilities and staff shortages, particularly in lower-income neighbourhoods.
The school demonstrations and blockades have morphed into larger protests over soaring living costs.

articles.title_orig: Hackers appear to be struggling to exploit PHP flaws after global cybersecurity crisis
articles.title_zh: Hackers appear to be struggling to exploit PHP flaws after global cybersecurity crisis
articles.content_orig:
Wiz Research uncovered multiple critical vulnerabilities in core PHP, a popular general-purpose scripting language that powers 70% of all websites in the world. Successful exploitation could allow attackers to take control of affected servers, steal sensitive data, and deface the websites running on them.
PHP is a backbone of the web: it’s the programming language powering WordPress, Joomla, Drupal, Wikipedia’s MediaWiki, and many others.
These vulnerabilities include memory disclosure and unauthenticated remote code execution in PHP itself, independent of the application running on top of it , putting every affected website in immediate risk.
Every PHP version released in the last decade is affected by at least one of these vulnerabilities, going back to version 5.4. Attackers can exploit them remotely, in some cases fairly easily. Immediate patching is strongly advised.
On October 21, 2026, PHP released the patch fixing multiple memory-safety vulnerabilities in the core engine.
These findings rank among the most severe vulnerabilities discovered in PHP, and arguably in software history. The underlying flaws had been present for decades, but demonstrating their exploitability  required an exceptionally complex chain of steps, at the edge of what human researchers could practically achieve. Frontier AI models substantially reduced that barrier, turning a longstanding flaw into an exploit.
In this post, we explain how frontier AI helped us find and fix vulnerabilities that had remained hidden in the PHP codebase for more than a decade. The issues described below all stem from key architecture decisions, some made over a decade ago, and were grouped under two CVEs, with severity reaching CVSS 9.2. The work grew into a cross-industry effort to protect customers, find variants, deploy detections and mitigations, and verify a patch in time for coordinated disclosure.
Nearly every PHP version is affected by at least one of these issues, including releases dating back to PHP 5.4. The vulnerabilities can allow unauthenticated attackers to execute code on affected servers or read sensitive process memory. That memory may contain passwords, authentication tokens, API keys and certificates belonging to other requests or the server itself.
PHP is the programming language behind much of the web, powering WordPress, Drupal and MediaWiki, the software that runs Wikipedia. A flaw in its core engine can affect websites across this ecosystem, even when their own application code is secure.
Some vulnerabilities become turning points because they challenge fundamental assumptions about security. In 2014, Heartbleed exposed the fragility of shared infrastructure securing the internet. In 2021, Log4Shell revealed how deeply embedded software dependencies could create widespread exposure that organizations struggled to identify. We believe PHP2Shell could mark a similar turning point for the AI era, illustrating how AI can change the practical exploitability of longstanding vulnerabilities. Building the exploit required chaining multiple flaws and adapting to each target’s memory layout through repeated testing and debugging. Frontier models were critical to making this process practical, enabling us to develop and adapt working exploits across multiple applications in hours. As the time and expertise required for this work decrease, complexity may no longer provide a meaningful barrier, changing how we define what is vulnerable in practice.
Wiz Research would like to thank the PHP team, Calif and OpenAI for their work on discovery, coordination and patch verification. OpenAI and Calif also published blogs containing details on the vulnerability – its history, technical details, and insight into the disclosure process. PHP posted as well.
We’d also like to express our sincere gratitude towards Automattic, Akamai, AWS, Cloudflare , Fastly , Google , Imperva, Microsoft, Vercel , and many others, for helping prepare guidance and out-of-the-box mitigations for customers who cannot apply the patch immediately.
All of the disclosed vulnerabilities are memory-safety issues that stem from bugs in how PHP handles fatal errors while processing requests, particularly out-of-memory errors. These bugs can leave a corrupted internal PHP state behind after a request ends unexpectedly. A later request or worker can reuse that stale state, leading to memory disclosure or corruption.
Below you can find a table that demonstrates what type of impact was demonstrated by each of the bugs we reported to PHP. The applications listed below are targets we chose for the RCE demonstrations. They are representative targets - exploitation does not require one of these CMSs, as the vulnerable code is in PHP itself.

While this blog covers only four instances of exploitable bugs (grouped under two CVEs) that follow this problematic pattern, there are other tracked, and likely untracked, variants of this issue in the PHP codebase. These variants have different requirements for exploitation and can lead to different types of impact. In any case, the patch provided by the PHP team fixes the issue at its core and eliminates all variants in the patched release.
We combined these vulnerabilities into a single exploit script, php2shell, and demonstrated that it could execute code remotely without authentication on deployments of WordPress ( wordpress:latest ), Drupal ( drupal:latest ), and Joomla ( joomla:latest ), using their latest container images at the time of testing.
These platforms illustrate the impact, but the vulnerabilities are in PHP itself. Exploitation does not depend on a flaw in the application’s code: even a simple “Hello World” application running on an affected PHP version can be vulnerable.
Separately, we demonstrated that attackers could read sensitive data from the PHP process’s memory, including passwords, tokens, and API keys, without needing to achieve remote code execution.
Demonstrations of PHP2Shell with Wordpress, Joomla, and Drupal:
The vulnerable code had been present for more than a decade. Turning these flaws into working exploits required chaining multiple bugs and accounting for how PHP allocates and reuses memory across requests. Memory bugs are notoriously complex; differences in PHP versions, configurations and application behavior can break assumptions the exploit depends on. An attack that works against one deployment may need substantial adjustments to work against another, each requiring further analysis, testing and debugging. Pre-AI, this manual work would be difficult to implement and even harder to scale.
With AI this is no longer a barrier. LLMs can help adapt an exploit to different PHP versions, configurations and memory layouts. With testing and debugging tools, models can analyze failures and iterate on adjustments, reducing the specialist effort required for each target. This significantly lowers the barrier to scaling attacks across different deployments.
This changes the economics of both discovery and exploitation. As AI reduces the effort needed to develop and adapt complex exploits, vulnerabilities that once seemed impractical to exploit become viable targets.
We used Wiz Atlas , Gemini 4 Argon and GPT-5.6 Sol throughout this research. Notably, Gemini 4 Argon made an invaluable contribution to finding the vulnerability, exploit development, attack detection, and validation of the patch.

articles.title_orig: Moderna shares sink after leaked cancer data missed expectations
articles.title_zh: Moderna shares sink after leaked cancer data missed expectations
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Two months ago, Moderna's ( MRNA ) melanoma vaccine handed the stock its best day ever. Now leaked results from the same trial have handed it its biggest intraday drop on record.
The stock fell as much as 26% before closing down more than 17%. That's still its worst day since Aug. 20, the session right after its best day.
This price reflects trading activity during the overnight session on the Blue Ocean ATS, available 8 PM to 4 AM ET, Sunday through Thursday, when regular markets are closed.
More than $17 billion in market value has vanished as details from the late-stage trial circulated ahead of their official debut . Merck ( MRK ), Moderna's partner on the vaccine, confirmed the results came out early. The full data is set for release Saturday at Europe's biggest cancer conference, in Madrid.
The leaked numbers are still good. The personalized vaccine, paired with Merck's blockbuster Keytruda, reportedly cut the risk of the cancer returning or death by 42%. An earlier, smaller trial showed 49%, though it used different patients, so it isn't a direct comparison. The bigger issue is how much the stock had already run, nearly quadrupling from mid-August to Wednesday.
Merck fell nearly 4% at its low before paring more than half the drop. The vaccine is central to Moderna's story, but it's just an add-on for Merck.
The rest of healthcare is rallied. Eli Lilly ( LLY ) is added more than $33 billion in market value, about twice what Moderna lost. Johnson & Johnson ( JNJ ) and Pfizer ( PFE ) rose, too.
The iShares Biotechnology ETF ( IBB ) and SPDR S&P Biotech ETF ( XBI ) were only modestly lower, roughly in step with the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ).
On Aug. 19, Moderna rocketed 177% to close at $174.38 after the company said the trial met its goals. It kept climbing from there, and on Wednesday, it posted its highest close since December 2021.
Thursday's low came within 4% of that August close before buyers stepped in. A sustained break below $174 would put $116 in focus. That's where trading opened on the record day.
Watch Saturday's full data, especially how lower-risk patients fared.

articles.content_orig:
Credit... Ofir Berman for The New York Times
Dr. Hardal is a co-director of A Land for All and a research fellow at the Shalom Hartman Institute in Jerusalem.
It is a bitter moment for the Palestinian citizens of Israel who will go to the polls on Tuesday. We are part of a national election in a state that is practicing the most devastating war, ethnic cleansing and violence against our people since the Nakba of 1948. Insecurity, after all, changes the meaning of political participation.
The attacks of Oct. 7, 2023, the war in Gaza and the political transformation inside Israel have forever altered the relationship among Palestinian citizens of Israel, the state and the Palestinian national question. Palestinian citizens are not only citizens of Israel; they are part of the larger Palestinian people whose experience over the past three years cannot be separated from what happens inside Israel.
Being a Palestinian Israeli voter is a paradox: We are asked to participate in a political system that does not treat us as an equal part of that democracy. Many of Israel’s political parties, including those seeking to replace Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, continue to resist the idea of an Arab party participating in a governing coalition. At the same time, some of them also understand that a high Palestinian turnout could help change the government .
In other words, our vote is important enough to affect the future of Israel, but most of the candidates still consider us to be unacceptable partners in governing. These questions became particularly urgent in September when Israel’s Central Elections Committee voted to disqualify the two Arab-majority parties from participating in this election. The Supreme Court overturned the decision, allowing them to run, though one candidate, Sami Abu Shehadeh, withdrew his candidacy after a public campaign against him.
Amid all of this, the daily lives of Palestinian citizens of Israel are growing more precarious. In recent years, organized crime has transformed life in many Palestinian communities: In 2025, 252 Arab citizens were killed in violent crimes — a record high. For many, the recent spike in crime is not simply experienced as a failure of policing. It is also seen as an expression of unequal citizenship and racist policies that exacerbate a long-held sense of state-led mistreatment. In the best case, we are seen as second- or third-class citizens; in the worst, we are enemies. The experience of abandonment is real.

Elon Musk has invested roughly $1 billion in Skydance, according to people familiar with the matter, providing a much needed financial injection as the company looks to cut costs and bolster its stock price.
The deal came together at roughly the same time as equity investments from Skydanceâs other investors, including board member Laurene Powell Jobs, the people said. Semafor reported in September that Paramount was considering seeking an equity injection from Musk.
Musk has publicly praised the Ellisons and Skydance, prompting speculation of a more expansive partnership between Muskâs lower-earth-orbit satellite network, Starlink, and Skydance.
âHeâs gonna have to re-engineer all of those channels, and figure out how they morph into streams themselves rather than just traditional linear,â billionaire cable executive John Malone said Tuesday. âI think thereâs a deal coming there,â Malone also said at his Paley Center appearance .
âWho helped Elon finance Twitter when he bought it? Larry Ellison,â Malone said. âHow did Larry Ellison come up with some of the money to put into the creation of Skydance? Tesla stock. And I would not doubt for a minute that before very long youâre going to see an announcement.â
A deal, in fact, had already come. Ellison, who poached Mattelâs Ynon Kreiz to serve as co-CEO, could use Muskâs capital to bolster the companyâs cost-cutting and technological efforts.
âWe are building a true product and tech team,â Ellison said in a CNBC interview earlier this month. âWe are a big believer that artificial intelligence is a tool for artists, not the other way around.â
Musk and Paramount did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
Musk was among a number of wealthy individuals that Paramount CEO David Ellison was considering working with for an investment.
Musk and David Ellisonâs father, Oracle founder Larry Ellison, have long been close, and it is in part the elder Ellisonâs money â and connections â that made Paramountâs takeover of Warner Bros. possible. Larry Ellison has personally guaranteed more than $40 billion of the equity financing for Paramountâs acquisition of Warner Bros.
Larry Ellison invested $1 billion in Muskâs 2022 deal to take X, formerly Twitter, private. He also invested in Tesla in 2018, and served on the companyâs board of directors for years.

Add Axios as your preferred source to
